P-1 after every sentence: 0 failures in all 8 runs; `ledger_mismatches` empty in all 8. Verification of every class (`verify_class`) and `replay_tower` were NOT run on these S300 towers (cost); they are in the tests on smaller streams.

### C3b open points (meaning-level; for the owner, nothing is decided by the code)
  (1) Under defer level-0 blacks fall to 0.74-0.85 of close (RUN low 560 -> 474, WORD low 1086 -> 891, RUN mid 437 -> 358, WORD mid 951 -> 656) and packs / levels shrink more at the top (WORD: 6 -> 4 and 5 -> 3 levels), but are still above C2's no-carry counts (RUN low 422, WORD low 676, RUN mid 319, WORD mid 524): the woken packs that DO fit still take seats. Black size grows slightly (median elements 6-7 -> 7-9).
  (2) The price: fewer packs wake (woken pairs roughly halve; distinct packs woken WORD mid 187 -> 91). Whether the lost wakings matter for answers is not measurable without the question side (C5).
  (3) Non-empty deferrals are not rare (264-1684 per run); about 70-80 % of non-empty pack collapses were ones the item alone fits. Under close those were 194-676 closes per run (RUN low 207 of 726 closes, WORD mid 676 of 1261 = 54 %) that came only from woken packs. Under defer 0 by construction; the rest of the closes are real.
  (4) Pack centres: the share of level-0 blacks whose class has a pack as a centre falls from 21-28 % to 17-19 % (RUN low 120/559 -> 85/473; WORD low 25 % -> 19 %; RUN mid 21 % -> 12 %; WORD mid 20 % -> 11 %); blacks whose centres are ALL packs stay rare (3-15). So packs are centres less often under defer, but not rare, and by this count the centre bias of the packs is not removed.
  (5) Time: defer cost more CPU at mid (RUN +22 %, WORD +62 %) because blacks hold more elements and the failed first attempt is paid every time; at low it is within noise.
  (6) Within a sentence, once a pack is deferred it can wake at the next vocab word, and then may be deferred again (a repeated failed attempt); the count of non-empty deferrals includes such repeats. Not counted separately.
  (7) The ledger does not mark whether a deferral was in an empty or non-empty black (the table classifies it with the spy, which is not part of the ledger); if the owner wants it in the ledger, that is an additional field (a header-format change for defer ledgers only).
  (8) The header key is written only for defer so that every C3 ledger stays valid and byte-identical; the cost is that "absent = close" is a convention in `check_cache_key`.

## T8e: stable-seats-path, one candidate per upper entry (verantyx/line3/matryoshka.py `candidate="stable-seats-path"`, CLI `--layer-candidate stable-seats-path`; default unchanged = `path`)
Binding: the owner's decision after T8d (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, 「T8d の測定後の決定」, verbatim choice 「席の並び、上の経路ごとに 1 候補」): the bundles lying on ONE upper-layer path (one upper entry) become ONE candidate, each bundle's restored stable state shown as its seat layout (centre + 6 arms); build and measure before it becomes the default. This is T8d open point (1) built. Everything not in that sentence is the most literal reading I could build, numbered, and listed as an open point. `path`, `bag`, `stable`, `stable-seats`, `stable-seated` and the default are byte-identical to 3f26068 (the existing golden hashes pass unchanged).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-430 | `LayerOptions(candidate="stable-seats-path")` / `--layer-candidate stable-seats-path`. The upper cross is read as before (so which bundles lie on which upper entry is unchanged). For each upper entry (an `AnswerEntry` of the upper read: its path words and its centre, the entry = one upper path / one word set as the upper read groups it) ONE candidate is built = the ordered list of its bundles, each with the seat layout of its restored stable state EXACTLY as stable-seats builds it (L-390 / L-392: the unchanged L-341 boundary, whatever step incl. 0, canonical-first arrangement, `down_read_seats` itself is reused unchanged). Candidate `words` = the sorted union of the words of its layouts. Record per candidate: `layouts = [{bundle, seats: {centre, arms, n_words, n_seats}}]`, `n_bundles`, `n_words`, `n_seats` (= sum of the layouts' seats; a word that sits in two bundles' layouts counts once in `n_words`, so n_seats can exceed n_words), `arrangements` (sum of the arrangements of the bundles' states), `path_from` (the L-342 boundary records), `word_sources`, `source_sids`. A bundle whose state gives no layout is left out of its candidate; an entry none of whose bundles gives a layout gives no candidate (counted in `entries_without_path_words`; 0 in the whole measurement). | matryoshka.entry_bundle_order, _read_layer, LayerEntry.layouts
| L-431 | Order of the bundles = the upper path's own order, as the upper read gives it, never sorted: the entry's arrangements in item order; in each arrangement the section paths in section order, each path's words as read, then the arrangement's centre; a bundle is listed at its first occurrence; bundles of the word set that no path or centre named (none expected) go last. The candidate stays an ordered list: two entries with the same bundles in a different order are two candidates. | matryoshka.entry_bundle_order
| L-432 | Equal candidates are one: candidates are equal iff their lists of layouts (structure of each seat layout, in order) are equal; bundles, centres, sources and path_from of equal candidates are merged, stability = maximum. A bundle appearing twice in one entry's order is listed once; two different bundles with the same layout stay two items of the list (not merged inside a candidate). | matryoshka._read_layer
| L-433 | Provenance and trace (L-394 extended): `word_sources` of a candidate = per word the union of the sources of that word in the layouts of all its bundles (seat_sources, L-394); `trace_run` unchanged: the words of the candidate = the words of `word_sources`, each source sentence holds the word, every word descends through one of the candidate's bundles to a base state, every restored state is a fixed point (L-343). Measured 100 % (every upper run traced, table). Layers >= 2: as L-393 (a seat shows the base seed word of its bundle). | matryoshka.trace_run
| L-434 | JSON / defaults: the new keys (`layouts`, `n_bundles`, `n_words`, `n_seats`) appear only for this mode (`seats` is absent: a candidate is not one layout); the entry's `candidate` = `stable-seats-path`; the boundary records are kept per run as in the other stable modes. cli.py: the flag's value list and help only. | matryoshka.LayerEntry.to_json_obj, cli.py
| L-435 | Cost: same reads as stable-seats (same cache keys); grouping adds nothing measurable. | matryoshka._read_layer

### T8e open points (meaning-level; not decided by the code)
  (1) Which upper entry = "one upper path": built as the upper read's entry (items with the same word set are one entry, L-180), so the candidate stands for all arrangements of that word set, and the bundle order comes from the first arrangement (item order, a label). A candidate per ARRANGEMENT (per item) would give more candidates with a fixed order each; not built.
  (2) The order of bundles is the first arrangement's section order (L-431); bundles that only appear in a later arrangement of the same word set come after. Whether the order should be the question's attached order, the order of path steps toward the centre (as built: outer word first, centre last), or reversed is the owner's decision. Two entries with the same layouts in another order are two candidates.
  (3) Words of a candidate = the union of the bundles' layouts, i.e. the same words as the T8 bag's candidate for that entry (gold set identical: 36 / 38); what is new is only the per-bundle seat layout, not the information. n_seats counts a word once per layout it sits in, so a long list of bundles makes a very large candidate (seats median 64, p90 491, max 1035 in standard): whether the user should read the layouts of all bundles or only those under the question's path words is not decided.
  (4) The per-path grouping gives the list shape of the bag (1 / 7 and 6 / 37 upper candidates per question in the bag; 1 / 15 and 12.5 / 44 here) and brings the first gold-holding candidate back up the list (standard median among the upper candidates 7 against 17 for per-bundle stable-seats), at the price of a single wrong answer on unanswerables (fast 1, standard 1; stable-seats 0): a candidate that is a list of layouts is still not tied to the question's path. Standard lists are 1.5 times the bag's (22 vs 15) because equal word sets with other layouts or another order stay separate (L-432).
  (5) A bundle with no layout is dropped silently from the candidate (never happened on S300): the alternative is to keep the empty bundle in the list.
  (6) T8d open points (2)-(9) and T8c / T8b / T8 open points are unchanged; the default stays `path`.

## C5: question answering over the tower (verantyx/line3/carry_query.py, tests/line3/test_carry_query.py)
Binding: docs/LINE3_CARRY_DESIGN.md 5.1-5.6, 6 (P-4), 9 (C5); owner's nesting answer (going up is a search shortcut: search the packs first, then only below the selected path), the T7 / T7b presets, the evaluation principle (candidates are for real users to grade; the 90-question score is not the goal). Takes a finished `CarryTower` (built under pack_overflow close or defer; only `units()`, `packs`, `carry`, `tier` are used). carry.py, placement.py, cycle.py, readout.py, trace_check.py, ask.py, cli.py untouched; cycle / readout / trace_check run unchanged on a per-unit read tier.

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-313 | Exact skip: rq(U) = sum over the distinct question units of the local sentences with a scope occurrence of that unit (an index lookup). rq = 0 -> not read: no question unit is in the unit's space, so no section works (N-03). `read_unit` reads without the skip; the test reads EVERY rq = 0 unit of a 40-sentence tower (5 questions) and finds no state / answer / entry, and compares the whole descent with and without the skip (same entries and verdict). | `rq`, `read_unit` |
| L-314 | Order = (level descending, rq descending); units with equal (level, rq) are one group, read together or not at all (never split); a group that does not fit stops the read (counted). Descents found in a group are applied after the whole group was read, so order inside a group cannot matter. A shuffled reference descent gives the same read set and entries (3 seeds). | `ask` |
| L-315 | Presets = `ask.EFFORTS` caps (fast 4 / standard 10 / full unbounded units, any level counts 1), QueryBudget(64, 8), never a rebuild; `nodes=N` as T7b. | `ask` |
| L-316 | Default descent = the packs on the paths of the ADOPTED states of the unit read (a unit with no adopted state does not descend). Flag `fallback="index"` = every pack seated in the unit read with rq > 0 (comparison only). | `ask` |
| L-317 | Candidates come from read level-0 blacks only; paths of upper units are in `thought` (reads, parents). | `_entries` |
| L-318 | An entry's sources = scope sentences of its black (global sids); an inherited pack is named `{"inherited": true, "pack", "unit", "is_centre"}`, never expanded into words. | `Entry.to_obj` |
| L-420 | Q = the question cut like the tier with the V2 filter (or `units`), distinct. Entrance = the open units of every level. | `question_units`, `ask` |
| L-421 | Read tier (`ReadTier`, a TierSpace over the unit's LOCAL sentences, `sids` = local -> global): postings of the seated elements; a question unit that is not an element (always above level 0, where elements are packs) gets postings from the scope occurrences of that unit, so the cycle can attach it and N-03 sees it; an element no scope occurrence touches (n = 0) is left out (L-52). | `read_tier` |
| L-422 | A unit's tied class (`Black.state`, no twin quotient) is given to `cycle._ask_tier_once(plan_override=...)` as a `Placement`; T7b defaults (V3 state rule, first-layer scope), `observe=False`, `member_cap` optional (None = all members). | `_UnitStore`, `read_unit` |
| L-423 | A unit reached from several read units keeps ALL parent links. The chain mark of a black = `entrances` + `links` (parent, pack, unit, lateral) = the backward closure of its links; a path list was built first and wrote 5.6 GB in one run of the index descent (exponential number of ways), so paths are read off the links. Lateral = the pack is inherited (woken) in the parent unit. | `_links` |
| L-424 | Entry merge across blacks: same (own word set, inherited pack ids) = one entry (T6z word-set rule; conservative about inherited packs); arrangements summed, centres / sources united, stability = best, one origin per black (chain mark, global sids, per-word sources). Entry keys = T7b's (tier, words, arrangements, centres, stability, source_sids, tier_is_most_stable [trivially true: one tower = one tier]) + `inherited` + `chain`. | `_entries` |
| L-425 | Verdict: 1 entry ANSWER, several CHOICE; none: UNKNOWN_NO_EVIDENCE (no question unit in any entrance scope: the skip left nothing to read), else UNKNOWN_NO_STATE (no read unit adopted a state) or UNKNOWN_NO_PATH (states, no entry). | `ask` |
| L-426 | Read counts as L-222: crosses_read (units), left_unread (queued, not allowed), would_read_in_full = INDEX count of units with rq > 0 (an upper bound of what the full descent reads), tied_group_not_split, reads per level, exact skips; `partial` = queue left. | `read_obj` |
| L-427 | P-4 `trace`, independent of the read-out: every entry word has a scope occurrence in its black; every source sid is a scope sentence (and, with the tier space, the global sentence holds the word); every chain link is a pack of the tower seated in the unit it leaves with the right lateral mark; every inherited element is in the black's copy; plus `trace_check.trace_answer` on each read tier. Tampering (foreign sid, unseated word, fake pack, flipped lateral mark, no entrance, wrong unit of an inherited pack) is detected. | `trace` |
| L-428 | `memory_record(i)` = the T7b record shape for the user's choice + `chain`; a list is never auto-adopted. | `CarryAnswer.memory_record` |
| L-429 | Output bytes carry no wall time and no float; byte-identical across PYTHONHASHSEED 0 / 1 / 12345 (test, and 7 S300 questions on a full tower). | `to_bytes` |

Tests: tests/line3/test_carry_query.py, 22 (with the three carry files: 99 passed). The design 5.5 example (hand counts: rq 1 / 1 / 1 / 0, entrance U1:0 and U0:2, U0:0 skipped with its lateral link, 3 units read, 2 entries, gold 山梨県 in the U0:1 entry, sources s2-s3 and s4-s5, inherited P1:0 / P1:1 named); skip = read over all units; order independence; presets, groups, partial counts; fallback superset; entry shape; P-4 (file and reversed stream order, so local sid != global sid); tamper detection; hash seeds; ladder of parents. Six mutants (skip too much, split a group, lateral mark, local sids, reversed priority, descent flag) each failed a test.

### C5 open points (meaning-level; not decided by the code)
  (1) The design's descent (search the packs on the selected path, L-316) loses the answer. [Review correction: "the upper units mostly adopt no state" was wrong. Close fast: level 3 adopts a state 73 / 73, level 2 41 / 78, level 1 9 / 11 (the other level-2 reads are UNKNOWN_NO_FIXED_POINT; 8x the query budget, QueryBudget(512, 64), turns 3 probed ones into SECTION / RATIO disagreement, not a state). The main loss is that the selected path does not pass through the pack that holds the question: on 10 probed questions U3:0 adopts ONE state whose path holds the same 13 packs for every question (1 leads to a unit with rq > 0), and where a level-2 / level-1 unit on the question's index chain adopts a state, the pack holding the question's sentence was on its path 0 of 2 times; exact skips 1526 in 90 questions. Some upper reads with rq > 0 end UNKNOWN_NO_EVIDENCE by the cycle's fall-through (no member kind), not by N-03.] In the 5.5 example U1:0 itself adopts nothing because its two packs tie and the tie abstains; a unit without a state, or whose path holds no pack with rq > 0, leads nowhere, so 63-71 of 90 questions end UNKNOWN_NO_PATH. Gold in a candidate 4 of 60 at every preset. The descent by index (every pack seated in the unit with rq > 0) gives 37 / 42 / 46 (close) and 43 / 51 (defer), more than flat (27 RUN only), but its descent is decided by rq (an index count, greedy per level), not by the search: it is closer to index retrieval than to the owner's "search the packs, then below the selected path". Which is the intended shortcut, and whether the upper unit should be read with a bigger query budget or by a rule other than the tied-abstain state, is the owner's call.
  (2) fast = 4 units cannot go down a 4-level tower unless each level contributes one unit (level-first order): the T7b caps were set for flat crosses. A cap in units per level, or depth not counted, is not decided.
  (3) The index descent gives mostly a SINGLE ANSWER (37 of 37 at close fast) because only the highest-rq unit per level is read: it looks confident; unanswerable single wrong 5-8 of 30 (flat RUN only 5). Lists appear only at standard/full.
  (4) Order among units uses rq (L-314); E_Q or another count is not tested.
  (5) Candidates only from level-0 blacks (L-317); upper-unit words are not shown. An entry holding only inherited packs would have no word (none counted as a problem in the runs but not asserted).
  (6) close vs defer on answers: defer holds more gold with the index descent (43 vs 37 fast, 51 vs 42 standard) and is faster (max 5 s vs 18-21 s: fewer, smaller units), but with the path descent both are ~3-4; single wrong on unanswerable 6-8 vs 5-6. The towers are built once (file order); order sensitivity (condition 3) of the answers is not measured here.
  (7) would_read_in_full is the index count (an upper bound); the true full-descent count needs the read. member_cap is None (every class member); one question took 203 s in the first (discarded) full-index run, before the chain closure replaced path lists (L-423).
  (8) The comparison with flat T7b / T8 is rough: one tier (RUN) at low vs three tiers pooled (flat) and layers; WORD / CHAR towers are not run.
  (9) Review: what the index-descent number measures (same towers, sha fe7ff3c699f1 / acd3ccf7d1ff; same oracle and 60 / 30 split as T7b; 5 rerun answers byte-identical). Trivial baselines with no cross read, gold in a candidate of 60: the level-0 black(s) with the highest rq, all words of their question sentences = 56 (close) / 57 (defer), one entry 56-57 times; the stream sentence(s) holding the most question units, all their words = 58. Every gold hit of the index descent (37 / 42 / 46 close, 43 / 51 defer) comes from that highest-rq black and is also a baseline hit; the cross read adds no hit, loses 6-19 (black not reached within the cap, or the black's read UNKNOWN_NO_FIXED_POINT / SECTION_DISAGREEMENT), and its entry is the whole question-sentence word set of the black (median ratio 1.00, close fast; 111 of 120 highest-rq blacks hold one sentence fragment of ~5 words). The centre word alone holds the gold 19 / 12 times. So 37-51 measures index retrieval of the subject's own sentence fragment (S300 holds each subject's defining sentence), not the search; "beats flat T7b" means the small level-0 black isolates that fragment better than a flat cross. The `lateral` flag of a chain is true when ANY link of the closure is lateral (the "gold through a lateral link" counts 3 / 7 / 5 can include chains that also have a non-lateral way).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-440 | `stable-seats-qpath` (Q1): of an upper entry, keep only the bundles on the section paths (of its arrangements) whose attached unit (`AnswerPath.attached`, the question unit on the section as the upper read attached it) is a question unit of the upper layer (the units the layer was read under); the arrangement's centre bundle is kept only if the centre itself is a question unit; bundles of other sections, and the bundles that the L-431 order lists last because no path named them, are dropped. Order = L-431 restricted to the kept bundles. | matryoshka.entry_qpath_bundles, _read_layer
| L-441 | `stable-seats-qword` (Q2): of an upper entry, keep only the bundles (L-431 order, all of them read down as in stable-seats-path) whose restored stable state (its seat layout, L-390) contains a question word. Question word = a question unit of the upper layer mapped down to base words by the existing down-mapping (`lower_units` applied `layer.k` times, i.e. the same units the lower cross is read under, `ul[0]`; at layers >= 2 a seat shows the base seed word of its bundle, L-393, so the test is on those seed words). A bundle with several states is kept per state that holds a question word. | matryoshka._read_layer
| L-442 | Candidate shape and provenance: as L-430 / L-432 / L-433 / L-434 over the kept bundles only: `words` = the union of the kept layouts' words, `layouts`, `n_bundles`, `n_words`, `n_seats`, `word_sources`, `path_from` (the boundary records of the kept bundles only; `boundaries` of the run lists every bundle read), `restored` for the fixed-point check of the kept states. The entry's `candidate` = the mode name. Two entries that end with equal kept layouts are one candidate. Every candidate is a subset, in the same order, of one stable-seats-path candidate of the same entry (tested). | matryoshka._read_layer, LayerEntry
| L-443 | An entry left with no kept bundle gives no candidate; it is counted in the new run field `without_kept` (JSON `entries_without_kept_bundles`, only for these two modes, next to `entries_without_path_words`, which keeps its meaning: an entry none of whose bundles gave a layout). 0 in the whole measurement. | matryoshka.LayerRun
| L-444 | Cost: qpath reads down only the kept bundles (fewer reads); qword reads every bundle as stable-seats-path does (same cache keys) and filters afterwards. | matryoshka._read_layer
| L-445 | cli.py: the flag's value list and help only (`--layer-candidate stable-seats-qpath|stable-seats-qword`). | cli.py

The old golden hashes unchanged; `entry_qpath_bundles` on a hand-built entry (kept = exactly the paths whose attached unit is a question unit, centre only if a question unit, order, empty set gives empty); for both modes the set of candidates of a run = exactly the set of (distinct) lists re-derived independently from the upper answer's items and the stable-seats layouts with the defined filter, nothing added or dropped; every candidate is an ordered subset of a stable-seats-path candidate of the same run; words = union of the kept layouts, sources and trace ok (fraction 1/1); JSON keys, no float; CLI accepts both values; PYTHONHASHSEED 0 / 1 / 12345 give equal bytes for both modes.

### T8f open points (meaning-level; not decided by the code)
  (1) Why Q1 changes almost nothing: every section path of an upper entry starts at an attached question unit by construction of the upper read (a section exists only for an attached unit), and every other bundle of the entry is a path word of such a path. So "the bundles on a path from a question unit's seat" is nearly all bundles of the entry; only the centre bundle (when it is not itself a question unit) and paths with no attached unit are dropped. Whether "under the question's path" should mean something narrower (for instance only the first word of each path, only the bundles within n steps of the question unit, only the path bundles that reach the centre, or the sections of the first six question units only) is not decided.
  (2) Q2's question words: built as the question units mapped down to their base SEED words (`ul[0]`, what the lower cross is read under). The other reading is every base word under a question bundle (`Layer.words[q]`), which is much larger and would keep even more bundles; not built. At layers >= 2 the seats show seed words, so the test sees only seeds (L-393).
  (3) Q2 keeps a bundle whose state contains a question word anywhere in its seats (centre or any arm, outer or inner); a stricter test (the word on the centre, or on the arm of its own section, or as the question's attached unit) is not built. Most restored states contain the question seeds because the lower cross is read under them.
  (4) qpath keeps the L-431 order of the kept bundles and does not re-sort; the centre bundle, when it is a question unit, is listed where L-431 lists the centre (after that arrangement's path words).
  (5) A bundle with no layout is dropped silently (as T8e (5)); an entry with no kept bundle gives no candidate and is counted (never happened). The alternative of keeping the entry with its first bundle, or of showing the unfiltered candidate when the filter empties it, is not built.
  (6) Making candidates smaller by this route did not work at the candidate level; the size of a candidate is set by the number of bundles the upper entry has (median 5 fast / 7 standard) and their layouts. Options not built: show only the layout of the bundle that carries the question word, cap the bundles per candidate, or show the words alone (the T8 bag) for the other bundles.
  (7) T8e open points (1)-(5), T8d (2)-(9) and earlier open points are unchanged; the default stays `path`.

## F2: answers that are not one unit, built from the connections between the granularities (verantyx/line3/granularity.py; docs/LINE3_F2_GRANULARITY.md)
Owner (T9 audit decision, 2026-10-08): 「そのために様じまな粒度での接続があるのでそれを使って」. Reading: the connection is the one the space already has (decision 2, I-01, L-03, L-32, L-212/L-213/L-220): the three tiers cut the SAME sentence, so a unit of one tier occupies a surface span of that sentence and contains the spans of the finer tiers' units inside it. No new mechanism, no n-gram joining, nothing scored or counted.

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-480 | Spans. `SpanIndex(space).spans(tier, sid)` = (start, end) of every unit of the tier in `strip_attribution(sentence)`, obtained by re-cutting the text with the tier's own splitter (RUN: content runs + letter-like gap pieces; WORD: fugashi surfaces; CHAR: letter-like characters) and removing the units the tier's function-word filter removed; the unit list must equal `TierSpace.sentence_units[sid]` or ValueError (no silent skip). Containment of spans across tiers is the connection. | granularity.py |
| L-481 | Joining. The occurrences (tier, sid, unit index) of the words of the listed entries in their source sentences whose spans overlap or touch are joined; "touch" = the characters between them contain no letter-like character (L-32: any character outside Unicode L/N/M, i.e. every character all tiers drop: 「・」「,」 and spaces, but also 「、」「。」「（」「）」「「」「」」; review: 29 of the 1176 flat strings and 119 of the 3024 path strings over the 18 questions join across one of 、。（）「」, and two seatsPath hits exist only through such a join: ウルトラプリニー式噴火（）、大, 73,921人（2007年). A joined span that one occurrence already covers is just an existing unit and is not reported. The result is the sentence surface [start, end) (the dropped middle characters stay), with its parts (tier, unit, span, entries). Ordered by (sid, start, end); no cap (N-20), no rank, no stability. | granularity._join / assemble |
| L-482 | Scope (OP-F2-1). `entry`: each entry alone; `all` (default): the occurrences of all entries of all tiers that point into the same sentence are pooled, so units of different tiers join (parts keep their tier and the entries they come from). The same span reached twice is one string with the union of the parts. | granularity.assemble |
| L-483 | Alignment. `aligned_tiers` = the tiers (RUN, WORD, CHAR order) whose units tile the string: both ends are unit boundaries of that tier and every letter-like character of the span lies in a unit of it; `lifted_tier` = the coarsest of them. Report only; nothing is chosen by it. | granularity._tiles |
| L-484 | `bridge=True` (OP-F2-2, off by default, library only): a gap whose letters all lie inside units that the RUN or WORD cut made and the function-word rule removed (の, から, ...) also joins. | granularity |
| L-485 | Hook. `ask.ask(..., granularity=None|True|"entry"|"all")`; `Combined.assembled` (new last field, default None) holds `granularity.assemble_combined(c, space, scope)` = {scope, n, strings[{text, sid, span, parts[{tier, unit, span, entries}], part_tiers, aligned_tiers, lifted_tier, entries}], rule}; it is built from `c.entries` (what the user is shown). `answer_obj()` gets the key `assembled` ONLY when it is set; the thought, the listed entries and every other byte are untouched. Off (default) = byte-identical (tested: bytes, answer, text). The parts stay listed; the string is an extra candidate (the owner's "use the connections", not "replace"). | ask.py (15 lines), granularity.py |
| L-486 | Text and command. `format_text` adds 「つなげた候補 N 件」 + one line per string (string, sentence #, span, aligned tiers, parts with tiers) only when set. `vera line3 ask --granularity entry|all` (default none); with layers on it is attached to layer 0 (the `base` of ask_layered), the layers' candidates get none (OP-F2-7). | ask.py, cli.py |
| L-487 | Traceability. `trace_check(space, assembled, bridge=False)` checks against the sentence text and the tiers' unit lists (no SpanIndex, no re-cut): string = sentence span; each part = unit `idx` of its tier = the span's surface, at the place of unit `idx` (the units before / after it fit before / after the span; review fix: a repeated surface at another place was accepted before) and inside the string; every letter-like character of the string lies in a part (or, with bridge, in a function-word unit); parts join through dropped characters only. [] = every character maps to the source sentence and to units of some tier. With bridge=True the function-word cover comes from SpanIndex (the assembler's own code), so that case is not independent. | granularity.trace_check |
| L-488 | Defaults and determinism: pure function of (space, entries); no float, no division, no set/dict-order dependence (sets are sorted before use; tested under PYTHONHASHSEED 0/1/12345). | tests/line3/test_granularity.py |

### Tests
tests/line3/test_granularity.py (26 passed after the review's added test; test_ask.py + test_readout*.py 62; together 88 passed): spans show the unit in every tier and a RUN unit contains the WORD/CHAR units inside it; ハッシュ表 (RUN ハッシュ+表, aligned RUN/WORD/CHAR), カール・マルクス (the 「・」 stays as surface), 最大3万2,500キロワット (split at the comma), no join across a letter, a lone unit adds nothing, bridge off/on; scope all joins WORD ハッシュ + RUN 表 (entry does not); a unit containing the other adds nothing; CHAR chain; same span from two entries; misaligned edges; trace_check on every string and on forged ones; default `ask` bytes/answer/text identical with no `assembled` key; option on = default answer + the `assembled` key only, the thought identical; hash seeds; no float.

This replays the post-processing on the recorded entries (identical to `c.entries` of an `ask` run with view=all, which pools the three tiers' layer-0 entries as the replay does); the T9 placement cache is not present on this machine and placement.py is being edited by F1, so `ask` itself was not re-run over the bank. Word-rule hits on all 69 are unchanged by construction (the option does not touch the entries; the T9 numbers are not recomputed by measure.py). Of the 18: **flat 4/18, path 4/18, seatsPath 11/18 (entry) 12/18 (all)**; hits by flat/path: I2-008, I2-019, I2-040, I2-047 (extra characters 0,0,0,2). Review: all four are adjacency of units of ONE tier in one sentence (RUN カール+マルクス, RUN BAN+BAN, a WORD chain トライデント..卒業, RUN 16の+国); the CHAR parts pooled by scope all lie inside them, so the cross-tier pooling adds 0 on flat/path (entry = all) and 1 on seatsPath (R2-I008, excess 4, through 「（）、」). The gold sentence is among the cited sources for 13/18 (flat), 15/18 (path), 18/18 (seatsPath); the full sentence is already shown in `sources`. Strings per question: flat median 26-31 (max 318), path 136-138 (max 513), seatsPath 1715-2235 (max 2752). | results.txt (2) |

So the flat/path 4 are signal (no false hits in the control). seatsPath is above the control (12/18 = 67 % vs 28 %; among the 14 assemblable golds 12/14 vs 86/238 = 36 %), but about a third of unrelated golds are also inside its 1700-2200 strings per question (mostly CHAR chains), so as a list it does not single out the answer. With bridge=True: flat/path 5/18, seatsPath 13-14/18, extra characters up to 31, control unchanged for flat/path (0/306) and 90-91/306 for seatsPath. | results.txt |
