### G3-d tests (tests/line3/test_slide_ratios.py; Pro, PYTHONHASHSEED 0 / 1 / 12345 identical)
45 tests. Hand toy windows (test_slide_place's corpus, window (0, 1)): T1 (東京 centre, 日本 -x, 首都 +z, 都市 -z; question 首都 東京): axis x ties (F_x = B_x = 89/377 for 東京 and 日本) and abstains with nowhere = edge, binding; axis z has F_z(東京) 89/1885, F_z(首都) 21/754, B_z(東京) 17/377, B_z(首都) 21/377 (plain B_z is a three-way tie, so the weight alone makes 首都 the binding's unit) = ratio_disagreement; axis y no_edges. T2 (首都 +x, 日本 -x): x AGREE on 東京 with F_x 877/1885, B_x 161/377, sources 1 + 2 rows. T3 (日本 +z, 都市 -z, 首都 -x; question 東京): z AGREE on 東京 (F_z 68/1885, B_z 17/377) while x abstains, i.e. the axes are judged separately. An asymmetric z edge from both ends; the independent route of the test (from geometry.neighbours, not edges) equals the reader on 5 crosses; the weight tests (only the edge terms move, sections / plain sums / other axes bit-identical, a common factor changes no decision, read order flips with the axis weights); the merged equality; 24 orientations (F, B invariant, the sections of an axis equal the window table); two seats keyed (unit, sid) with and without the z self edge; the real slide_place record in the G3-c configuration (= T1) and in the module default (two seats), all members; the question attachment; trace; bytes; no float; nothing hooked. Exhaustive: an axis with ONE evidenced edge never agrees (all ordered pairs of units x 6 arms x n 1..3 x 12 questions of 0..2 units, 10 000+ cases).
Fulllead, first pair windows (informational, not a measurement of the model: the "question" is the window's own first one or two units, no bank question; at most 4 members per window): 60 windows, G3-c configuration, 704 member reads: slide:x answers in 30 reads (10 per question form), no slide:z answer, y always no_edges; the invariants (merged equality, trace, determinism) hold on every real cross read. Time: placement 0.29 s per window (0.60 s in the two-seat default), reading + merged check 3 ms per member.

### G3-d open points (owner; meaning level)
(1) The weight is PER ARM (+x の 144 and -x に 89 weigh the two sides of one axis differently), as G3 3.5 (1) reads it ("腕 a の辺の項に r_F(p_a) を掛ける"). Inside an axis this is a bias toward the +side (T1: the plain z binding is a tie, the weighted one picks 首都). If the weight were per AXIS (w(+a) + w(-a) on every edge of a) it would be a pure scale inside an axis and could change no decision, only the read order. The owner's words (「重みは辺の流れと配置の結合と読む順に」) do not say which. (2) Structure: an axis with ONE evidenced edge can never agree (exhaustively tested; algebra: R1 on the centre needs E(C) >= E(O), R2 needs E(O)/n(O) > E(C)/n(C), R3 needs n(C) < n(O)), so agreement needs at least two evidenced edges on the axis, and for z it needs a unit on each z arm with z evidence (the G3-c record, 338 of 1000 z-arm units have none). Together with the weights this is why agreements are rare in the first measurement (x in about 4 % of member reads, z none). Is that the intended strictness, or should the three ratios of a single edge be allowed to agree (e.g. R1 not required to stop on the same side)? (review, 2026-10-09) "Never" is too strong: the algebra above reads ONE energy E for R1 and R2, but R1 reads E_q of the section's attached query unit (L-59) and R2 reads E_Q. It holds when some section that sees the edge's arm reads E_Q, and for every question of at most 3 units (window 3: the arm's three sections then carry the whole query, and the sum of their three walk conditions gives E_Q(C) > E_Q(O), against R2); the exhaustive test used questions of 0-2 units only. With 4+ units it fails: C in 4 sentences, O in 5 (one shared), a b c only with C, d only with O, question a b c d, O on -x: the three -x sections carry a b c and walk O -> C, d pulls E_Q to O (9/40 > 7/32), n(C) < n(O): one evidenced edge, AGREE on C (test_one_evidenced_edge_can_agree_when_every_section_of_its_arm_reads_an_attached_unit). Rare, not impossible (0 of the single-edge axes in the 20 bank2 windows of the review). The background line of the owner's decision after G3-d (「決して一致しない（代数と全数試験）」) rests on the narrower statement. (3) The self z edge of a unit with two seats (the owner counted it in the key): should it count in F_z and B_z (option `z_self_edges`, default off = energy.py's L-56)? With it on, the unit with two seats is the only unit with z flow and its axis agrees by itself. (4) Is N-03 per axis (an agreeing axis answers only if one of ITS working sections has an in-space query unit attached), or global as in the cycle? Recorded (`grounded`), not gated. (5) A class of equal-key arrangements gives different per-axis ratios (G3-c open point 3): which member answers, the most stable one per axis (as L-107) or one for all axes? `read_members` lists the agreeing members per axis and breaks no tie. (6) "The section ratio value" of an answer: built as the largest energy at which the working sections' walks ended on the unit (E_q for attached sections); the owner's three "ratio values" are energies/flows, a walk has no ratio of its own. Another reading (a count of working sections, or the energy under the whole query) changes only what is printed, not the agreement. (7) y is structurally empty (no_edges) until the two-tier pack (G3-h); the y machinery is the same code and reads counts.y when a cross has two tiers (the unit would then need a tier on its seat).

### G3-d addendum (2026-10-09): owner decisions on the G3-d open points (verantyx/line3/slide_ratios.py; tests/line3/test_slide_ratios.py)
Owner (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, 「G3-d の実装後の決定」): both single-edge rules are to be measured; weights stay per arm; the z self edge counts by default. L-615 `read_axes(..., agreement="three" | "two_if_single_edge")`, default "three" (= L-606 unchanged). "two_if_single_edge": an axis with exactly ONE evidenced edge (both ends seated, n_a > 0, not a same-unit pair that is skipped) is judged on R2 and R3 only (AGREE iff both point to the same unit, else points_nowhere / ratio_disagreement); its section walk is skipped and recorded as not applicable (`section_applicable` false, no sections, `section_unit` None, the answer's `section` value None, no walk steps, `grounded` 0, "section" never listed in `nowhere`); axes with 0 or 2+ evidenced edges are read exactly as under "three" (tested for equality); the rule is in the bytes (`agreement`). L-616 `z_self_edges` default is ON (L-604 changes only its default; `merged_check` fixes it to False because energy.py's L-56 skips same-unit pairs, so the merged equality of 7.3 is unchanged); the weights stay per arm (L-605 unchanged). Tests: 51 (6 new: the switch on T1 and T3, a single-edge axis that answers under the new rule only (centre 東京, 首都 on +x, question 都市: F_x 216/1885 vs 144/1885, B_x 144/377 vs 144/754), an exhaustive single-edge sweep (no answer under "three"; under the new rule an answer exactly when R2 = R3, other axes unchanged), two-edge axes alike under both rules, the z default); the two-seat test now compares the default (on) with an explicit False. (review, 2026-10-09: 52 tests; +1 the single-edge counter-example with a 4-unit question; the exhaustive single-edge test is renamed to what it shows (questions of 0-2 units); the two-seat adapter test also reads the record's jsonl form and compares the bytes under both agreement rules.) Open (meaning): under "two_if_single_edge" a single-edge answer rests on two ratios that by construction pull in opposite directions in many cases (R3 prefers the unit of small n, R2 the unit of high E per n); the measurement of both rules should report how often each axis answers and how the answer agrees with the evidence sentence.

## G3-c2 (2026-10-09): the owner's decisions after G3-c as spec switches of the window placement (verantyx/line3/slide_place.py; tests/line3/test_slide_place2.py; tests/line3/test_slide_place.py fixture; experiments/line3/g3/place2/)
Owner (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, 「G3-c の実装後の決定」 and 「G3-c の監査後の決定」, verbatim choices): 「記事ごとに仮の文を 1 つ足す（合計 892）」; 「軸ごとに別々に判定し、各軸がそれぞれ安定を持つ」 (合計の鍵ではなく、各軸で改善が無いときに安定); 「両方を比較する」 (証拠の無い軸の腕に座らせる版と座らせない版を S1 で並べて測る); 「文ごとに席を分ける（同じ語が 2 席、z の辺でつながる）」; 「z の腕は N+1 の語専用にする」 (x の腕は文 N、z の腕は文 N+1). One module is extended (slide_place.py) and one new test file added; placement.py, slide.py, slide_ratios.py (G3-d, written concurrently, reads the record below) and every other module are untouched; nothing imports slide_place from ask / cycle / matryoshka. The G3-c behaviour is ONE named configuration (`SP.LEGACY`) and is byte-identical to the committed G3-c records; the owner's configuration is `SP.DEFAULTS`. Judgement points are numbered from L-580 (L-573..L-579 are unused; G3-d took L-600..).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-580 | Four spec switches, defaults = the owner's configuration, G3-c = `LEGACY`. `stability` "sum" (G3-c) / "per_axis"; `seat_key` "unit" (G3-c: one seat per unit) / "unit_sid"; `seat_empty_axis` "allow" (G3-c) / "deny"; `growth` "n_then_n1" (G3-c) / "interleave" / "z_reserved". `DEFAULTS` = per_axis, unit_sid, allow, z_reserved (per_axis became the default because LEGACY is reachable byte-identically, tests below; z_reserved is the owner's 「z の腕は N+1 の語専用」; allow is kept because the owner said "両方を比較する" and measured results are below). `make_spec(..., stability=None, seat_key=None, seat_empty_axis=None, growth=None)`: a switch left at None takes the default; `make_spec(slide, **SP.LEGACY)` is the G3-c spec. A fourth switch beyond the ticket's three (`seat_key`) is needed because decision 4 changes the arrangement of every window with a shared unit (81 of the 292 windows seat a unit with n_z(u, u) > 0, L-570) and the committed records would otherwise be unreachable. The spec doc lists the switches (and the rule texts) only when they differ from LEGACY, so the LEGACY spec keeps its G3-c bytes and its sha256 (tested equal to the G3-c module's). The low-level `grow(...)`, `verify_fixed_point_slide`, `verify_class_slide`, `min_L` default to the G3-c behaviour (keyword switches `stability`, `z_reserved`, `arm_names`, `sides`), so the G3-c hand tables read unchanged. The only edit of the G3-c test file: its spec fixture and the 8 `SP.make_spec(` calls go through `mk_spec(slide, **kw) = SP.make_spec(slide, **dict(SP.LEGACY, **kw))` (a file that tests G3-c asks for the G3-c configuration); its 29 tests pass unchanged. | slide_place.LEGACY / DEFAULTS / PlaceSpec / make_spec |
| L-581 | Per-axis stability = PARETO. The key of an arrangement is split by axis, (n_x, omega_x), (n_y, omega_y), (n_z, omega_z), each axis compared lexicographically as in G3-c. A single move is IMPROVING when no axis falls and at least one rises ("an arrangement whose per-axis keys are all >= is better"); it is EQUAL when no axis changes; a move that raises one axis and lowers another is neither (so a move improving x and worsening z is not taken, a move improving both is). A state is a fixed point when it has no improving move. The summed key (sum n_a, sum omega_a) is still computed and recorded (`key`) but is no longer read by the decision. Why not the most literal reading ("no move improves key_a on ANY axis", so a trade-off move also makes a state unstable): a trade-off x up / z down and its inverse z up / x down would each make the other state unstable, so a search with that rule can cycle and need not have any stable state at all; Pareto is the weakest rule under which every climb terminates (product order on a finite set) and which still makes each axis "have its own stability" (an axis that rises while none falls is never given up for another). The strict reading, lexicographic (x, then y, then z) and weighted readings are open point 1; `tradeoff_counts` measures how often they would differ (below). On windows with only x (one-sentence windows: no z, y never has an edge) the rule is the G3-c rule (tested equal: toy and 12 fulllead lone windows). | slide_place._vflags, _vdom, _maximal, _scan_pa |
| L-582 | The per-axis search (G3-c's L-561 machinery with a partial order). `_scan_pa`: of the improving swaps keep those whose axis-delta is not dominated by another improving swap's (the Pareto-maximal ones; ties and incomparable ones all branch, as G3-c's "best" ties did); `_settle_pa`: climb, keep the terminals whose per-axis key no other terminal's dominates, close each key's terminals under the no-axis-changes swaps (an escape = an improving swap from a member, as before), climb again from the escapes of a class that has any, and return the union of the closed classes whose key no other closed class dominates; `_insert_one_pa`: a unit goes to the empty allowed seats whose gain 6-vector is not dominated by another seat's (incomparable gains branch). Consequence: a class may hold SEVERAL INCOMPARABLE per-axis keys (record: `axis_splits` > 1 and `axis_split_set` lists every key with its member count; measured: 57 of 292 windows under n_then_n1, 0 under z_reserved); `one_key` need not hold, the verifier checks an antichain instead (L-589). The max_class budget keeps counting closure additions per key class only, exactly as G3-c's `_settle` (the defect noted at L-561 is NOT fixed here, a separate task does: 7 windows end with a class above max_class under per_axis n_then_n1, 10 under interleave, 0 under z_reserved). The G3-c functions are kept as they were (copied algorithm, `sum` path) with one added optional argument, the seating policy, so the sum path is byte-identical. | slide_place._scan_pa, _settle_pa, _insert_one_pa |
| L-583 | `seat_empty_axis="deny"`: an arm whose axis has ZERO evidence in the window has no seats. Evidence of an axis = any count of the axis for pairs of the tier's units in `slide.counts` (x: a shared sentence, y: a containment between the tier's units, z: a unit of N with a unit of N+1); `axes_with_evidence`. In S1 y never has any (one tier: no y edge), so the y arms are seatless as before; in a one-sentence window the z arms have no seats (no N+1: no z count at all); a sentence pair whose sentences hold one unit each has no x. The arms of denied axes are listed in `seatless_arms` (the record also lists `axis_evidence` {x, y, z}); `min_L` uses the reduced number of arms (2 L + 1 for the x arms alone, so a 7-unit one-sentence window gets L = 3 where "allow" gives L = 2); `min_L` is None when no arm has seats and more than one unit comes (the growth then stops with reason "no_seat", L-586). The PER-UNIT variant (a unit may sit on an arm only if it has at least one edge of that axis) is NOT built (open point 3). allow = G3-c (a z arm of a one-sentence window holds fillers at zero gain). | slide_place.axes_with_evidence, arms in place_window |
| L-584 | `seat_key="unit_sid"`: a seat is keyed (unit, sentence). A unit that occurs in both sentences of the window gets two seats, one per sentence: tokens `unit + SEP + sid` (`SEP` = "\x00"; units of one sentence keep the plain unit as token), `Item(token, unit, side, sid)` with side "this" (sentence N) or "next" (N+1) -- "both" no longer occurs. The edge weights stay the unit-level corpus evidence (`ArmWeights` reads a token as its unit, `unit_of`), so the two seats of one unit are linked by the z self-edge n_z(u, u) wherever they sit next to each other on a z arm or through the centre (n_z(u, u) is symmetric: +z and -z weigh the same), and have no x edge (n_x(u, u) is not defined: 0). The z weight does NOT look at the sentence of the seat (it stays "the corpus counts windows with o in N and i in N+1", L-G3-1: seats from the window, evidence from the corpus); gating the weight by the seat's sentence would also change seats="unit" and is open point 6. All provenance is per seat (L-587). `next_seat` (strict / loose) is read on seats: STRICT = a seated unit only in N+1, LOOSE = a seated N+1 seat (a shared unit's N+1 seat included, its N seat no longer counts), so LOOSE is not comparable with G3-c's (71.5 % there). `z_self` stays (seated units with n_z(u, u) > 0, once per unit) and `self_links` is new: per unit with two seats its n_z(u, u), whether both are seated and whether they are the two ends of ONE cross edge (and on which arm). Under "unit" the old rule holds (one seat, side "both", sid = the sentence where it is first read). Classes are larger under "unit_sid" (the two seats of a unit are exchangeable at equal key). | slide_place.Item, seat_items, unit_of, _self_links |

"n_then_n1" (G3-c): all of N in word order, then all of N+1 (a unit's first occurrence in its sentence; under "unit_sid" a shared unit appears in both lists). "interleave": N's first, N+1's first, N's second, N+1's second, ... (the longer sentence continues alone; under "unit" a unit already read is skipped, so a unit first read from N+1 is seated with sid N+1 and side "both"). `seat_items` builds the order for all three (with seat_key "unit" and n_then_n1 it equals G3-c's `insertion_order`, tested). | slide_place.seat_items |

The reservation binds INSERTION (a seat goes only to an allowed empty seat) and EVERY SWAP (a move that would put a seat on an arm it is not allowed on is not a move; an empty seat takes anything) -- both in the per_axis and the sum search (`Policy`, `_swap_legal`). Capacity: the arm length L is the smallest at which Hall's conditions hold for the seats inserted so far (tokens of N <= 1 + x seats + y seats, tokens of N+1 <= 1 + z seats + y seats, all <= all seats), and then grown until every class member has an empty allowed seat for the new token: the arms GROW (the literal reading; stopping instead, as at a budget break, would conflate the reservation with the F1 stop); a seat for which no L helps (all its arms denied) stops the growth with reason "no_seat" (recorded like a budget break, `left` lists the rest). One consequence is measured (open point 4): the z arms hold only N+1 seats, so a +z arm (whose edge weight reads "outer in N, inner in N+1") holds them in the reversed direction. ### G3-c2 open points (owner; meaning level)
(1) Per-axis stability is built as PARETO (L-581): no axis falls and one rises. The strict reading (a state is stable when NO move improves ANY axis) cannot be a termination rule (a trade-off and its inverse alternate; stable states need not exist); alternatives: lexicographic in the ladder order x, y, z (decide by x, only then by z), a weighted sum with the foundation weights (233 : 89 : 34), or the strict reading used as a test only (`tradeoff_counts`: how many single moves of the representative improve one axis and worsen another: 374 of 12913 under n_then_n1, 22 of 13830 under z_reserved). Which is the owner's 「各軸がそれぞれ安定を持つ」? (review, 2026-10-09) Pareto is the implementer's constructive choice, not the literal gloss: 「各軸で改善が無いときに安定」 reads as the strict condition (no move improves any axis). The non-termination argument is about a SEARCH rule; as a stability JUDGEMENT the strict condition is a well-defined predicate on a state and is already measured: a Pareto fixed point with no trade-off move (`tradeoffs.improve_one_worsen_another` = 0, verifier `swaps_tradeoff`) is also strictly stable. Representatives that are: 274 of 292 under z_reserved (run 4), 189 of 292 under n_then_n1 (run 1). A third reading (each axis its own arrangement, judged by its own key alone) does not fit one cross per window and is listed only.
(2) A per-axis class can hold several INCOMPARABLE per-axis keys (n_then_n1: 57 of 292 windows, up to 4 keys; interleave 86, up to 5; z_reserved none). Is a class with two keys one answer (keep all members and let G3-d read each) or should a rule pick one key (which needs a preference among axes, point 1)?
(3) `deny` is the axis rule (an arm of an axis with no evidence in the window has no seats). It only matters for the 300 one-sentence windows (z) and, under z_reserved, not at all. The per-unit variant (a unit may sit on a z arm only if it has at least one z edge, on an x arm only with an x edge, ...) is not built: with it a seat could not be a filler on any arm; 570 of 994 z-arm units have no z evidence on the inner edge in run 1 (407 on neither edge). Build it?
(4) z_reserved and the direction of z. The +z arm's edge reads "outer in N, inner in N+1" (G3 3.2), the -z arm "outer in N+1, inner in N"; with the z arms reserved for N+1 seats the centre (a sentence-N unit) is the inner end of the innermost seat, which is the -z reading, and the +z arm holds N+1 seats in the reversed direction: 15 of 306 seats on +z have z evidence on their inner edge, 282 of 647 on -z (and beyond the innermost seat both neighbours are N+1 seats, whose z edge counts only by corpus coincidence). Options: reserve +z for N seats and -z for N+1 seats (then x and +z both hold N), flip the +z weight for N+1 seats, or give the z arms one direction only. Not decided here. (review, 2026-10-09) By depth (run 4, representatives; the centre is a sentence-N seat in 292 of 292): -z depth 1 (inner = centre, the only N -> N+1 edge of the cross) 236 of 236 evidenced (the window's own pair always counts in corpus scope; 7 of them self-edges); +z depth 1 9 of 129 (its weight n_z(o, i) needs the pair in the reversed sentence order elsewhere: 3 self-edges, 6 coincidences); deeper z seats (N+1 -> N+1 edges) -z 46 of 411, +z 6 of 177 (corpus coincidence). So the z axis holds at most one real slide edge per window, and 192 of 292 windows have exactly one evidenced z edge (56 none). The section walk starts at the OUTER end (L-55): in the 20 review windows (owner configuration, bank2 questions) the 120 z-arm walks stop 81 on an empty outer seat and 39 on an unproven N+1 -> N+1 step, 0 reach the centre, so R1_z cannot work. Further options: z arms of depth 1 (one N+1 seat per z arm), deeper z edges weighed by the word order of N+1 (an x-type count), or the centre may also be an N+1 seat.
(5) z_reserved lets the arms GROW until the reserved arms hold their sentence (L up to 8 on the pairs, 10 on a one-sentence window of 21 units since only the two x arms may hold N): arm length is not bounded by the budget. Alternative: stop when the reserved arms are full (like an F1 stop, `left` listing the rest), or bound L. Which is meant by "z の腕は N+1 の語専用"? (review, 2026-10-09) The growth is the literal consequence of the reservation, one arm length for all arms and no stop (not a slip); its only bound is `bound = len(order) + 2` in `grow` (never reached when a seat exists: at L = len(order) every allowed arm has room), an unnumbered cap. Longer arms leave the z arms' outer seats empty, which is where the section walk starts (point 4).
(6) The two seats of one unit have the same unit-level weights except for their mutual z self-edge: their sentence changes where they may sit (z_reserved) and in which order they are inserted, not what an edge weighs. Should an edge's z weight depend on the seats' sentences (a +z edge needs the outer seat in N and the inner in N+1)? It would be a different key (and change seat_key "unit" too).
(7) Interleave: 99.3 % strict and 53.7 % of N+1's seats seated, but 154 windows still die inside N and 10 end with a class above max_class; z_reserved: 80.8 % strict, 56 die inside N. Neither fixes the budget (214 of the 220 stops of run 1 are max_class on classes of tied fillers): a larger level or the quotient over interchangeable seats (the twin quotient of L-90 is not applied, L-561) is the structural cure; the max_class defect (a class can end above max_class) is a separate task.
(8) The search is local (swaps only; a Pareto fixed point is weaker than a summed-key fixed point, which is itself not the optimum, G3-c open point 5). Is a Pareto fixed point enough as "placed"?

## G3-c3 (2026-10-09): the centre in either sentence, the arm length measured both ways, stability judged strictly (verantyx/line3/slide_place.py; tests/line3/test_slide_place3.py; tests/line3/test_slide_place2.py one fixture; experiments/line3/g3/place3/)
Owner (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, 「G3-c2 の実装後の決定」 and 「G3-c2/G3-d の監査後の決定」, verbatim choices): 「中心も N+1 の語になれる（中心の探索を両文に広げる）」 (the centre is searched over the units of both sentences; with the centre in N+1 the x arms are N+1 and the z arms are N: symmetric); 「両方測ってから決める」 for the arm length ((a) grow until the budget stops, (b) as long as the x arms); 「厳密：どの軸にも改善する手が無いときだけ安定」 (the search stays Pareto, only the judgement is strict; an axis that still has an improving move means unstable = not judgeable). One module is extended (slide_place.py) and one new test file added; placement.py, slide.py, slide_ratios.py, ask.py, cli.py, slide_query.py (G3-e, written concurrently) are untouched. The record only gains fields (`NEW_RECORD_FIELDS_C3`); `record.seats` (unit / sid / arm / position / sources), `axis_keys`, `items`, `self_links`, `tradeoffs` keep their meaning. Judgement points are numbered L-620.. (L-600..L-616 are G3-d).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-620 | Switch `centre_scope`: "n" (G3-c2: the first unit of N is the centre and the centre moves by search among what the reservation allows) | "both". "both" only has a meaning with growth `z_reserved` (without the reservation the centre already moves freely; the switch is then a recorded no-op, tested). **The centre cannot move between sentences by a swap**: with x arms reserved for one sentence, swapping the centre with an arm seat of the other sentence leaves every other seat on an arm it is not allowed on (that is why run 4 shows the centre in N in 292 of 292). So "search the centre over both sentences" is TWO GROWTHS per two-sentence window: growth N (centre = first unit of N, x arms = N, z arms = N+1, order N then N+1; the G3-c2 growth) and growth N+1 (centre = first unit of N+1, x arms = N+1 in its word order, z arms = N, order N+1 then N). Inside a growth the centre moves by swaps among its own sentence's units (it takes only a unit of the sentence its x arms are reserved for, or a unit of both under seat_key "unit": `Policy.centre_only`); the N growth no longer lets an N+1 unit sit at the centre (G3-c2 allowed it; it never happened). A one-sentence window has one growth. | slide_place.PlaceSpec.centre_scope, place_window, Policy.centre_only |
| L-621 | The reservation is mirrored, not rewritten: `Policy(x_side="this"|"next")`. x arms take the units of `x_side`'s sentence (or "both"), z arms the other (or "both"), y arms any, as before; capacity (Hall's conditions) exchanges the roles (centre's sentence <= centre + x + y seats, other sentence <= z + y seats when the centre is closed to it, all <= all seats). `grow(..., x_side, centre_only, cap_x)`; `seat_items(..., centre="next")` reads N+1 first (all of N+1 in word order, then all of N). `side` of an item stays the corpus fact (this = N, next = N+1), so `record.seats`, `items`, `slide_ratios.window_cross` need no change (checked: `slide_ratios.window_crosses` reads a centre-in-N+1 record, members included). With seat_key "unit" a unit of both sentences is seated when first read, so its `sid` is that of the sentence read first in each growth; `items` (and `order_log`, `seat_order`) of the record are those of the REPRESENTATIVE's growth (review fix: they were the N growth's, so a centre-in-N+1 representative carried N's insertion order beside the N+1 growth's `steps`); under seat_key "unit" a shared unit's `sid` in `items` / `seats` is therefore that of the sentence the representative's growth read first, and the members of the other growth in the same record are read through the same `items` (seat_key "unit" is not the default; under the default unit_sid the two growths have the same tokens and sids, only the order differs). Per-weight nothing changes: with the centre in N+1 and N on the z arms the +z edge (outer in N, inner in N+1) is the right-directed one and -z the reversed one, the exact mirror of run 4. | slide_place.Policy, grow, seat_items |
| L-622 | The merge. The final classes of the two growths are compared member by member on the per-axis key (6-vector of L-581): a member is kept unless a member of the OTHER growth's class dominates it; equal keys keep both; incomparable keys keep both (`choice` "this", "next", "both_equal", "both_incomparable", "single"). ### G3-c3 open points (owner; meaning level)
(1) Which growth is "the best centre"? The two final classes are compared by their per-axis key although they may have seated different numbers of units (they differ in 186 of 292 windows) and a growth that stopped early has fewer edges. 106 windows keep both (15 equal, 91 incomparable: one growth is higher on x, the other on z) and the representative is then the N growth by the order rule, which is arbitrary: the "centre in N+1" share is 74 of 292 as representatives, 180 if a window counts when any member has the centre in N+1. Compare on equal footing (same seated set), prefer the growth that seated more, or ask the key's axis preference (G3-c2 point 1)?
(2) The symmetric centre answers the DIRECTION of z, not the NUMBER of cross-sentence edges. With the centre in one sentence and the z arms holding the other, the only N<->N+1 edges are the two innermost z edges (centre to the depth-1 seat of +z and of -z): median 1, max 2 in every run, 51 windows none (D: 56), 138 two (D: 129). Depth-1 z edges now carry evidence in 52-74 % (D: +z 7 %, -z 100 %: the centre in N made -z the only right-directed arm); the deeper z edges are N->N or N+1->N+1 pairs and carry evidence only by corpus coincidence (9.5-13 %). So the z axis still holds at most two slide edges. Precisely: the y arms hold no seat, so every edge joins two adjacent seats of one arm or an arm's innermost seat and the centre; the x arms and the centre hold only the centre's sentence and the z arms only the other sentence, so the only edges whose ends are seats of different sentences are (centre, +z depth 1) and (centre, -z depth 1): at most two per member, whichever sentence holds the centre and under either arm_cap (checked on the records of runs A-D: 0 such edges anywhere else). Options: (a) accept (the z axis is structurally a one-or-two-edge axis; G3-d's single-edge agreement rule is then the z norm, not the exception); (b) deeper z edges carry the other sentence's word-order evidence (an x-type count of the other sentence on the z arms); (c) more than one centre-like link between the sentences (e.g. several seats of the centre's sentence that open a z edge, or a z arm that alternates the sentences); (d) z arms of depth 1 only (one seat of the other sentence per z arm); (e) both z arms holding the other sentence in both directions.
(3) arm_cap x vs budget (A vs B, same search otherwise). x skips units of the other sentence that do not fit: 351 units in 52 windows (18 %); it halves the class (median 426 -> 216, windows above max_class 16 -> 7, 438 s -> 353 s), keeps the strict share (82.5 % both), seats fewer other-sentence seats (810 vs 875) and raises the z-evidence share (37.4 % vs 34.8 %); the representative stability is the same (94.1 vs 94.5 %). The cap is hard when the centre's sentence is short: a 2-unit centre sentence gives L = 1 and two z seats, whatever the other sentence has. Which is meant by 「x の腕と同じ長さまで」: the length the centre's sentence needed (built), or the length of the seated x arms after the search (often shorter), or a ratio? Decide before it becomes the default.
(4) Strict stability: 16 of 292 representatives are not strictly stable in A (all on z; D 18), but 15 of those 16 windows have a class member that is: a representative chosen among the strictly stable members would abstain in 1 window instead of 16 (97.4 % of all members pass). Is the unit of judgement the representative (built: `unstable`), the class (all members), or "some member" (`first_stable_strict_member`)? A trade-off move is one the Pareto search refuses on purpose (z down for x up); calling the state unstable for it means abstaining where the arrangement is a legitimate Pareto optimum.
(5) The merged class is the union of two growths' classes: up to 2079 members (16 windows above max_class 1000, D none): the budget counts each growth, not the union (the max_class defect of L-561 is still a separate task).
(6) The shorter growth is padded at the outer end (L-623): its outer seats are empty and a reader that walks from the outer end (R1_z, G2 section walk) starts on an empty seat in 89 growths more than before. Cap x gives shorter arms (L median 4 both) only when it bites. Should a record keep one record per growth instead of one merged L?
(7) Budget stops still decide most outcomes: 175 of the 186 budget stops in A are max_class on classes of tied fillers (D 187 of 195); 135 representatives stop inside the OTHER sentence and 51 inside the centre's. The structural cure is still the quotient over interchangeable seats (L-561, G3-c2 point 7).
(8) seat_key "unit" with centre_scope "both" (shared units seated once) is built and tested but not measured: a shared unit's `sid` is that of the sentence read first, which differs between the two growths.

What the numbers say (the facts; the reading is the owner's):
- windows read: fast reads 4 windows at the median of 6 candidates; 44 of the 69 questions are partial and 3 read nothing (the first tied block is larger than 4); standard / full leave 14 / 0 partial and add one or two hits, so the cap is not what limits S1.
- Between "seated" (40) and "agreed" (0-2) the loss is in the agreement (review: 40 is counted over every candidate window, no cap; at fast a gold window is READ for 28 of them, the other 12 are lost to the cap first — the grammar order reads the slot's group first: for I2-002 / I2-012 / I2-027 / I2-028 the 4 windows read are the same 4 of the と group, which hold only 呼 of 呼ばれますか): under `three` 2 entries in 94 questions at fast (the 69 answerable questions' (window, axis) pairs: section_disagreement 134, points_nowhere 91, ratio_disagreement 28, mixed 102, y always no_edges 294); under `two_if_single_edge` 164 of the 166 entries (94 questions) are on z — the answer is an end of the ONE real N -> N+1 edge — and they depend on the arrangement: only 2 of the 166 are agreed by every member of the class (`unanimous members only`: 0 hits, 0-5 entries), 3 of 166 are a question unit, 63 are the window's centre, 61 of 166 have a question unit on their path; `grounded` is 0 for 164.
- the other golds are rarely held either (chance: another question's gold in an entry 0.3 % per other question): the entries are mostly units nobody asked for.
- unans: `three` abstains 25 of 25 at fast (the typed verdicts: ratio disagreement 21, section disagreement 2, no evidence 1, not read 1); `two_if_single_edge` gives 7 single confident answers at fast (5 at full) — it breaks "no single confident wrong answer" on the questions that have no answer.
- time: 94 questions in 10-12 s wall with 6 workers at fast; 0.54 s per question at the median (all members), 0.10 s with representatives; the window build is 39 s once.
- the exact skip on the real corpus: 94 / 94 questions equal, 637 windows read instead of 55648; 1878 entries (about 20 per question, 94 of 94 questions) would have come from windows that hold no question unit.

### G3-e open points (owner; meaning level)
1. S1 as specified gives no usable answer: gold in a candidate 0 / 69 at fast for both agreement rules (2 / 69 at full under the two-ratio rule) against 16 for flat-fast and 21 for ssp, with 40 / 69 golds seated in a read window. The loss is the agreement (and, under the two-ratio rule, the arrangement): is the next step a different rule for the z axis (an answer must lie on an evidenced path that starts at a question unit's seat, like T8f's qpath; unanimity over the class; a z edge only counts when it has more than one real N -> N+1 edge), or S2 (y: the WORD units and the stand-ins) before judging the windows?
2. `agreement`: `three` abstains on the unanswerable questions (25 / 25) and answers almost nothing; `two_if_single_edge` answers 28 / 69 questions with a list and gives 7 / 25 confident single answers on the unanswerable ones. The principle (no single confident wrong answer) and the owner's two-ratio idea pull apart on the same data: which one is S1's rule?
3. A window's answer depends on the arrangement of its class (median 3 members, max 960). Listed: any agreeing member (`arrangements` = how many). Alternatives: every member must agree (unanimous: nothing is left), the share as the order of the list, or one arrangement chosen by stability (L-107). Which?
4. `words = [unit]` (one unit, I-11) cannot hold a gold that is several units (18 of 69 are not one unit of any tier; "ハッシュ表" is RUN ハッシュ + 表): the diagnostic `unit+path` gives 2 / 4 at fast / full. Should the entry carry the section-path words (T6w's form) as `words`, as T7b's entries do?
5. The cap counts windows in whole tied blocks, and a block larger than the cap reads nothing (3 of 69 answerable questions read nothing at fast). The within-group key (question units held, L-645) is this ticket's own choice for L-G3-7's "E_Q descending". Reading none of a too-large first block, or splitting it by the number of question units, or reading it anyway?
6. The admission gate (L-646) is a rule: without it windows that hold no question unit answer about 20 times per question. The same question applies to a candidate window: its entry is a unit that the question may not touch (61 of 166 entries have a question unit on their path). Should an entry require a path from a question unit?
7. `stable_strict` / growths (L-648, L-658) now follow the owner's decisions; not measured here because the S1 run is on committed G3-c2 records. Open: on G3-c3 records many windows may become window abstentions (on the toy, 1 of 9 windows has no stable member and 1 has 2 of 8), and every extra growth member is read; the S1 run should be repeated on a G3-c3 cache (`sweep.sh` with a new cache dir, about 1 minute) before the numbers above are used for a decision.
8. The grammar form selects only the match group (form `slot`: 25 of 94 questions) and the axis order; `predicate` (50) and `standin` (17) questions are read in ladder order, like `plain` (L-642). The 両替機 reading may need more than a read order (OP-G3-5): which form should select what?

### G3-e review (2026-10-09, Opus): why the agreement loses the 40 seated golds (member 0 of each gold window; `three` / `two_if_single_edge`; `experiments/line3/g3/s1/gold_loss.py` -> `results/gold_loss.txt`, run on the same G3-c2 window cache; rerun it on a G3-c3 cache with the S1 sweep)
Cause of the gold instance closest to agreeing, per question, the cap counted first at fast: cap (no gold window read) 12 / 12; the section walk passes the gold and ends further in (at the centre, an energy drop or an unproven step) 9 / 9; the gold's arm walk is `empty` (its OUTER seat is empty: G3-c2 fills a short arm from the centre outward, and `_Reader.walk` starts at position 0; 533 of the 1511 seated arms of the 592 windows) 6 / 5; the gold is on a z arm with no evidenced z edge (both ends in N+1: 536 of the 588 outer z edges have n_z = 0; only the edge to the centre carries N -> N+1) 5 / 6; the gold is on the z arm's one evidenced edge 5 / 5; R1 = gold but R3 elsewhere 1 / 1; section disagreement that includes the gold 1 / 1; the walk stops before the gold 1 / 1; the strict-member filter 0 / 0 (the G3-c2 records carry no flag). Without the cap (every candidate window): walk passes the gold 17 / 13, z one evidenced edge 8 / 6, outer seat empty 6 / 5, stops before 3 / 3, section disagreement 2 / 2, gold at the centre with no walk reaching it 2 / 2, R1 = gold 1 / 1, z no evidence 1 / 6, agreed on the gold 0 / 2 (= the 2 hits at full). Up to 40 members per window: no member of a gold window agrees on the gold under `three`; 2 questions under the two-ratio rule. Counterfactual (not a proposal): starting each walk at the first seated cell recovers 0 golds. R2 or R3 points to the gold in 11 of the 40 questions, both in 3. Two-ratio rule at fast: 16 single wrong answers on ANSWERABLE questions too (the table), besides the 7 on unans of open point 2. The binding loss is R1's form: a walk ends at the centre or at a break, so a gold in the middle of an arm, or on a z arm away from the centre, is never R1.

## G3-c4 (2026-10-09): the deeper z-arm edges measured under two evidence rules, `z_deep` "slide" | "order" (verantyx/line3/slide.py `SlideSpec.z_deep`, slide_place.py, slide_ratios.py; tests/line3/test_slide_place4.py; experiments/line3/g3/c4/)
Owner (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, 「G3-c3 の実装後の決定」, verbatim): 「両方測ってから決める」 for the evidence of the deeper z-arm edges ((a) 今のまま: 奥の辺はスライドの辺として数え、ほぼ証拠なし; (b) 奥の辺は向こうの文の語順の証拠（x と同じ数え方）を持つ), 「両方を候補として残す（同点は一覧）」 for the windows whose two centre growths are incomparable, 「類の中で厳密に安定な並びだけを読む」 for the unit of the strict judgement. The last two are already built (G3-c3 L-622 / L-658 keep both growths and list their answers separately; G3-e L-648 reads only the strictly stable members), so this ticket builds the first only. Three modules are extended (slide.py, slide_place.py, slide_ratios.py) and one test file added; placement.py, ask.py, cli.py, slide_query.py (G3-e, committed b1e42873 while this ticket ran) and test_slide_query.py are untouched. The default (`z_deep` "slide") is byte-identical: the committed G3-c3 run-A records of the first 40 pair windows, the G3-d toy ratios and the slide spec sha are reproduced (tests). Judgement points are numbered L-660.. (L-640..L-658 are G3-e).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-660 | The switch is the SLIDE spec's: `z_deep` "slide" (default: every z-arm edge is a slide edge, evidence n_z) | "order" (only the innermost z edge is a slide edge; a deeper one carries the pair's word-order count). It is a parameter `deep` of the z axis definition (`default_spec(space, z_deep=...)`, property `SlideSpec.z_deep`, validated by the supported-values table) and exists in the spec document ONLY under "order" (with a sentence of the axis text), so the default spec keeps its bytes and sha256 and "order" has another one; the place spec carries the slide spec sha, so it changes too, and so do the window cache file names (`slidewin_<corpus>_RUN_<slide sha12>_<place sha12>.pkl`). `Slide.counts` stamps the rule on `WindowCounts.z_deep` (new field, default "slide"; the counts' document lists it only under "order"), so that every reader of a window's counts (the placement's weights, the verifier, the ratio reader, slide_query through `counts_evidence`) takes the rule from the one place that was made under the spec; no signature of an existing function changed. Harness consequence: `slide_query.WindowIndex.from_space` builds `SL.Slide(space, rows=rows)` with the default spec, so the S1 script cannot reach the switch; `experiments/line3/g3/c4/measure_c4.py` is a copy of S1's measure_slide.py that replaces `slide.default_spec` for its process (`--z-deep`), the fork workers inherit it, and nothing in slide_query.py / measure_slide.py was edited (open point 4). | slide.default_axes / SlideSpec.z_deep / WindowCounts.z_deep, Z_DEEPS |
| L-661 | What "deeper" means. Positional, from the layout: the INNERMOST z edge is the edge whose inner end is the centre (centre <-> the depth-1 seat of a z arm); every other edge of a z arm (both ends are seats of the arm) is DEEPER. ### G3-c4 open points (owner; meaning level)
(1) Neither rule moves the gold into a candidate: gold in a candidate 0 / 69 in all four configurations at fast (S1 on G3-c2: 0 / 69; reach 40 / 41 of 69), so the loss is still the agreement step, not the evidence of the deeper edges. In the 73 (slide) / 78 (order) windows that seat the gold, only 91 / 19 of 16966 / 7528 member-axes agree on any unit under `three` (x: 19 / 12, none the gold). What changed is the mix: on the z axis points_nowhere 42 % -> 20 %, section_disagreement 40 % -> 47 %, ratio_disagreement 7 % -> 9 %; on x nothing but fewer members (the classes are smaller). Which part of the agreement is to be examined next: the section walk (every working section must point to one unit; the sections attach to question units, I-07), the question units that the gold windows hold (V1), or the x axis of those windows? This ticket does not touch any of them.
(2) What "the other sentence's word order" is counted over. Built: the pair's x count over the counts' scope, exactly as an x arm reads it (scope corpus: every sentence that holds both units; two units of one sentence therefore always have n >= 1, so the deeper z edges carry evidence in 1144 of 1144 cases and the information is only the size of n and the direction p(o, i)). The other reading, the order inside THIS window's other sentence (n = 1, direction known from the sentence), would make every deeper edge of the same weight and direction-only; it is a different count (scope window of x restricted to one sid) and is not built (L-667). Also the rule is positional: without growth z_reserved a deeper edge can join a unit of N and a unit of N+1; it then reads the pair's corpus order count, which is not "the other sentence's" (all measurements here use z_reserved).
(3) The growths are compared by a key whose z entry now mixes counts (L-662): the representative's centre in N+1 falls 74 -> 17 of 292, windows that keep both growths rise 106 -> 249 (the cause is not analysed); units seated rise 67 % -> 79 %, class size median 426 -> 101, budget stops 186 -> 115. The G3-c3 open point 1 (compare growths on equal footing) is therefore more pressing under "order", not less.
(4) `two_if_single_edge` no longer differs from `three` under "order" (identical entries and verdicts on all 94 questions): with a deeper edge the z axis has two or more evidenced edges, so the single-edge rule (G3-d 「辺が 1 本の軸」) did not change a single entry or verdict on the 94 questions at fast (a window whose z arms have L = 1 has no deeper edge and could still have exactly one evidenced z edge); under "slide" it is what produced the 111 z entries (and the 9 confident wrong answers on unans). So the owner's choice of evidence rule for the deeper z edges also decides whether z answers at all: order 5 entries over 94 questions, slide `three` 6, slide `two_if_single_edge` 113.
(5) Not comparable with S1: S1 ran on G3-c2 placements; the `c3 placements, z_deep slide` rows are the first S1 numbers on G3-c3 placements (G3-e open point 7): gold 0 / 69 as before, single wrong 2 -> 6 (three) and 16 -> 14 (two_if), unans abstained 25 / 25 and 10 / 25.
(6) Citations: the tag of L-665 keeps the order rows out of `slide_query._sids_of` (it reads z rows by their integer sids), so an order-rule z answer cites its seats' sentences and the innermost edge's (N, N+1) only; the sentences whose word order is the evidence of every deeper edge are in the answer's `sources` rows but not in `source_sids`. If the answer must cite them, `_sids_of` needs a case for the "order" tag (G3-e's file). (7) `z_deep` is not an argument of `WindowIndex.from_space` / `ask_slide` / `ask.py` / `cli.py` (G3-e's files): the S1 script reaches it through `slide.default_spec`. The switch should go through `WindowIndex.from_space(..., slide_kw=...)` (or `z_deep=`), recorded in the cache header and in the answer's `spec` shas (already different).

For a member that agrees on unit u on axis a: the section walks of `slide_ratios.AxisRatios.sections` whose section unit is u and whose terminus is u (exactly the walks `AxisAnswer.walk_steps` is taken from; each distinct (arm, path) once), `AxisWalk.path` read outer end first, ending at the centre or at the break. `words` = the units of those walks, walk after walk (section order, then arm order), each unit once at its first occurrence. With two arms of the axis ending on the same unit the union reads arm 1 (outer to u), then the other arm's units that arm 1 did not hold, the centre being where arm 1 reached it (toy: 猫 魚 食 for 魚 on x). PROVENANCE PER WORD (`word_provenance`, aligned with `words`): `basis` "walk", the arms it was walked on, its seats on the walks (unit, sid, arm, position, occurrence rows: the cross's own, as the entry's `seats`), the walk steps that arrive at it (arm, from, to, n, source rows, rule) and the sentences of both (`source_sids`). The walks used are in the entry (`walks`: arm, stop, path as (unit, sid) pairs). ### G3-e2 open points (owner; meaning level)
1. The shape does not reach the golds because the agreement decides which unit answers, and a unit-level agreement (R1 = R2 = R3 on the END unit) is the wrong gate for a path: the gold is on the path of a walk in 31 / 34 of 69 questions and agreed in 1. Is the next step a path-valued agreement (a walk is a candidate when it is a working section's walk, its edge flow or binding as an order only; or every working walk of an axis whose terminus unit the three ratios do not contradict), i.e. a different rule for what answers, not a different display?
2. Under `two_if_single_edge` the one-edge z axis (the bulk of the entries) has no section walk, so the path is the one unit (L-681). Should its path be the edge (both ends, outer to inner), as the flat readout shows a seat's neighbour, or the end unit only?
3. The entry shows the path of its first agreeing member and lists the others in `path_variants` (L-682). Alternatives: the union of the agreeing members' paths (one candidate, longer), or one entry per distinct path (more entries: tried first in this ticket, 26 entries from 4 unit entries on slide three, 12 per list; dropped because it multiplied the lists).
4. Two arms of an axis that end on the same unit give a union in which the centre sits between the arms (猫 魚 食, L-681). Is that the intended "outer to centre" order, or should the arms be listed apart (the `walks` field already has them)?
5. The new read order still leaves 28 of the 69 questions reading the full 4 windows and 44 partial; 2-3 questions read nothing because the first (most question units) block is larger than 4. Splitting that block, reading it anyway, or a larger fast cap are the earlier open point 5 of G3-e, unchanged.
6. `two_if_single_edge` on z_deep slide: 8 of 25 unanswerable questions get a single confident answer under any shape and order; this is the agreement rule, not the shape (G3-e open point 2).
7. Citations: the order-rule rows of z_deep "order" are not in `source_sids` (G3-c4 open point 6, L-688); under "path" the provenance sentences are.
8. The measurement is on the G3-c3 placements of the working tree (the G3-c4 slide.py / slide_place.py / slide_ratios.py were under review while this ran): if the reviewer changes the placements the cache shas change and the sweep must be rebuilt (`sweep_e2.sh` builds a missing cache; the numbers above are on caches with the shas named). Review: G3-c4 is now committed (0db1f585) and the `code_sha256` of all nine e2 runs' .meta.json equals that tree's slide.py / slide_place.py / slide_ratios.py / ask.py / grammar.py, and slide_query.py is this ticket's file as reviewed (the review changed one comment after the runs), so the numbers are on the committed placements.

Judgement points are numbered L-700.. (L-680..L-688 are G3-e2). The reading is the owner's; this is the build and the measurement.

What it is. The window index, the question intake, the read order, the cap, the member choice and the member cross are slide_query's (imported, not copied; committed in fd75b222, G3-e2: every run's .meta.json records its sha, 3b17519d...). Each strictly stable member of a window's class becomes a START (a flat tuple of units, centre + 6 arms, cycle.py's world-view state); the starts of one window are read as the members of one cross by `cycle._ask_tier_once(..., plan_override=...)` with a duck-typed carrier (`FlatCross`: seed, L, members, twin_sets): every start is settled by the T5 moves (23 rotations + seat swaps, key I-12), the answering end states are pooled and adopted by the V3 rule, `readout.read_out_result` reads the path words into T7b entries (merged sections, entries = word sets), `trace_check.trace_answer` traces every word. cycle.py, readout.py, trace_check.py, energy.py, geometry.py, slide*.py, grammar.py are not edited. The per-axis answers of slide_ratios on the placed members are attached to each entry as labels.

One call per window; the window's starts (all arm lengths) are its crosses, so the V3 adoption (the end states of all answering starts, the ones sharing the most sentences with the question) pools both centre growths of a window and never pools across windows (a window is a cross, and crosses of one tier are read separately, I-16; the entries of different windows are never merged, as slide_query). `member_rule` stable_any, `state_rule` query_share, `scope` first_layer, function / question words dropped (V2): cycle's own defaults, nothing overridden. `observe=False`: the energy log of the adopted states (design L-20) is not produced (it is a thought-object item the entries do not use). | slide_flat.read_window_flat |

### G3-f open points (owner; meaning level)
1. Confident wrong answers. A window is a small cross: one entry is an ANSWER. Flat rep gives 5 / 25 single answers to unanswerable questions at fast (4-6 on the other rows; T10 0-1) and 5 wrong against 3 right among the answerable; evidence window 10 / 25 and 17 against 5. The evaluation principle is "no single confident wrong answer". Should a window read ever be an ANSWER alone (rule: a single window's single entry is shown as a list of one with the abstention counts; or an ANSWER needs the same word set from two windows; or the verdict of a flat read is always CHOICE)? Not decided here: the verdict rule is slide_query's / ask.combine's (one entry = ANSWER).
2. The budget. The flat rows of T10 ran under QueryBudget(64, 8) (L-210); that budget settles none of the window starts (0 / 69). The window rows run under cycle's own 512 / 64 and do not compare like for like with 16 / 19. Which budget (states per start? crosses?) is the same amount of inference for a 7 x 6 + 1 seat cross and for a 3 x 6 + 1 one, and is a larger budget worth its AMBIGUOUS (tied branches ending in different results; the cycle abstains, L-106) rather than NO_FIXED_POINT? 4096 / 512 changed no gold.
3. evidence plain (the owner's "like T10") against window (L-714). Plain reads the corpus tier's n_pair on every edge, so the slide (z) evidence of an edge is not read by the flat reader (387 of 577 z-arm edges evidenced, 50 of 240 at the centre); window sums the window's x, y and z counts label-blind, which puts the slide back, doubles the golds (9 -> 19 at fast) and more than doubles the confident wrong answers (5 -> 17 among the answerable, 5 -> 10 among the unanswerable), changes the E_Q of pack pairs (design 8: the E_Q formula is unchanged, its pair input is not) and is traced against a tier with constructed pair sentences (16 % of the edge words). Should the owner's decision be read as plain, window, or neither (a separate evidence rule per arm label is impossible in the flat reader: it has no labels)?
4. Labels. Attached on the PLACED member (the start), not on the end state (the flat cycle moves units off their arms: a label of an end state would be a label of another cross). In every FLAT rep row the per-axis answers of the placed members agree for almost no entry (14 of 1796 entries, agreement three), so they say "disagree" on the entries that hold the gold. Are labels still wanted, with agreement two_if_single_edge (`label_agreement`), or on the end state?
5. members all or representative. The representative (the first member of each growth) is 696 starts for 592 windows; all strictly stable members is 103183 (the default of `ask_flat` is all; the measurement uses the representative). On the 57 questions run: members all with evidence plain reads 8 of 40 golds (243 entries in the lists; single wrong 3 of 40, 4 of 17 unanswerable) against the representative's 5 (18 entries; 3; 2 of 17); members all with evidence window reads 20 of 40 (489 entries, median 10, max 65; single wrong 2 of 40, 4 of 17 unanswerable) against the representative's 13 (42 entries; 7; 8 of 17), and T10 flat RUN-only reads 11 of 40 (773 entries; single wrong 1 of 40, 0 of 17). A question costs a median 77-84 s with all (max 1488 s) against 1.3 s. Which one is the product default; or a cap on the starts (`member_cap`) per window; the other 37 questions and standard are not measured.
6. Two seats. A unit of both sentences keeps both seats (L-703); the flat reader does not count the z self-edge n_z(u, u) that slide_ratios counts since G3-d (L-56), and a path may list the unit twice. `n_only` is measured (8 of 69; 3 single wrong of 25). Is the owner's "count the self-edge" (G3-d) meant for the flat reader as well (it would change cycle.Reader, not this module)?
7. Hook. `ask_flat` is not behind `ask(structure=...)` / the CLI (slide_query.py, cli.py, ask.py were the G3-e2 reviewer's files); the follow-up adds `structure="slide_flat"` (or replaces the per-axis reading as `slide`) and the options (`--members`, `--two-seat`, `--evidence`, `--budget`).
8. Everything is fulllead; S3000 and the held-out set are not read (the held-out folder was not opened). The 94 questions are the ones the earlier S1 / T10 rows used; one run each (the reading is deterministic: the same bytes under PYTHONHASHSEED 0 / 1 / 12345).
9. slide_query helpers are imported: `WindowIndex`, `intake`, `plan_windows`, `choose_members`, `member_cross`, `Plan`, `Intake`, `verdict` constants. A change of their signatures breaks this module's tests.

### G3-f tests, files
tests/line3/test_slide_flat.py: 36 tests (35 + the review's member_cap test): equality with cycle + readout on a hand cross held by a real placement.Placement (one start for two members that differ by a permutation of the legs; the same entries, citations and search digest), equality on the real toy windows (with shared units: entries only, a real Placement counts a cross with a unit twice wrongly), strictly stable members only / `strict="mark"`, pad cut, member-level V1, slide counts = tier counts (n_x == n_pair, before_x == p_pair on every pair of every toy window), two seats (both / n_only, centre never emptied, a unit twice on a path is a word once), labels decide nothing (labels off, labels replaced: same verdict, entries, bytes except the label), the label is slide_ratios' read of the placed member (independently recomputed), entry shape, both growths pooled, typed abstentions, the verdict precedence, V1 / cap / read order are slide_query's, representative + `growth_members`, evidence window (the sum of the counts, shared n and postings, the trace tier, equality with cycle on the WindowTier, the switch changes the reading, the default is plain, `constructed_edge_words`), PYTHONHASHSEED 0 / 1 / 12345 byte equality in five configurations, no floating-point number (AST) and no float in the output, the trace on the window tier holds and a corrupted state fails it, slide_query's bytes unchanged, `ask_flat` through an ask.Index. 88 tests pass with tests/line3/test_slide_ratios.py (52) after the review. Experiments: experiments/line3/g3/s1flat/ (measure_flat.py, sweep_flat.sh, summarize_flat.py, edge_evidence.py, trace_share.py, subset_ids.py, equiv_check.py; results/ the final runs with .meta.json (argv, config, shas, cache files), results_pre/ the earlier runs of the equivalence check and the six questions of the first members-all attempt).

All six window rows (plain and window, fast and standard) together find 28 golds, all six T10 rows together 28, the union 37: 9 golds are found by a window row and by no T10 row (I2-002 I2-004 I2-006 I2-024 I2-030 I2-042 I2-043 I2-045 R2-I018), 9 by a T10 row and by no window row. Six of the nine (I2-004, I2-006, I2-024, I2-030, I2-042, I2-043; all from evidence window rows) are the case the slide was built for: the question's subject is in sentence N (花園町駅, 海浦駅, 近江八幡郵便局, 中之嶽神社, 五十嵐浜村, 宮床村) and the gold in N+1 (Y17, OR08, 集配普通郵便局, 16柱, 新潟市西区, 大和町); the other three (I2-002, I2-045 one-sentence windows; R2-I018 gold in N) come from plain rows and are not a crossing.

Confident wrong answers (open point 1), by cause: every single answer is one entry of one window (entries are never merged across windows). Plain fast: of the 5 single answers to unanswerable questions, 3 are partial reads (UF-010 read 1 of its 11 candidate windows, UF-016, UF-020) and 4 had other windows read that abstained with a typed kind (UF-008 is the only one whose single window was all it had). Window fast: 10 single answers to unanswerable questions, 5 of them from a question that read exactly one window (UF-004, UF-010, UF-012, R2-U003, R2-U004), 3 partial. The ANSWER rule (one entry = ANSWER) sees neither the cap (`partial`) nor the sibling windows' abstentions.

Judgement points are numbered L-720.. (L-700..L-715 are G3-f).

### G3-g open points (owner questions; behaviour decided only as written above)
  (1) Merge scope (L-721). One entry per word set across tiers, layers and windows departs from L-220 (a same word set in two tiers is two entries) and from L-700 (never merged across windows). Measured effect: small (median 0 fewer entries at fast, 8 at standard; no ANSWER arises from a merge; of the 27 / 60 multi-origin entries 25 / 58 are the two window variants agreeing, and two per preset cross families). Is the cross-source merge wanted as it is, kept only across origins (L-700 restored inside a window origin), or replaced by something that shows containment (a short window set inside a long flat set), which "never merged across different word sets" forbids? Review note: the recorded decision says only 「1 つの一覧に並べる（出所のラベル付き）」; the cross-source merge is not derivable from it (L-235 merges inside one layer run and keeps labels apart; L-220 and L-700 keep two entries). No switch for an unmerged list is built (it would run merge -> combine -> ask_combined -> ask -> CLI); nothing is lost meanwhile: every entry keeps every member with its origin, so the unmerged list is the members in list order, a display choice, not a rerun.
  (2) Order (L-720). The fixed order puts the windows last, so a gold only windows find stands at position up to 120 of 122 behind the flat and layers entries, although the windows list 2-17 entries and the flat part 28-60 (median). No ranking was added (I-14). Windows first, one block per family with a header, or a per-family display cap are product choices; the data (origin on every entry) allow any of them without a rerun.
  (3) Length. The owner's list has median 28.5 / 60 entries and up to 147 / 227 (median 484 / 1956 words) at fast / standard, nearly all from the flat cross and the layers (T10's lists); it never is a single answer, so the gain over B1 / B2 (31 / 20 single right answers) is nil and a user must read a long list to reach 29 / 34 of 69 golds against B2's 57.
  (4) No abstention. No question is answered with an empty list but one at fast (1 of 94); the unanswerable ones are 25 / 25 rejectable lists, 0 confident wrong. The typed abstentions per source are there (`abstention_counts`), but the combined verdict is CHOICE whenever any source lists something. Whether a question that only the window-evidence variant lists (the weaker P-4) should be marked more strongly than the entry mark is open.
  (5) Weaker P-4 of the window-sum evidence (L-714): 106 of 147 (fast) of its entries hold a word evidenced only by a constructed pair sentence; the mark `window_evidence_variant` is on every such entry, and the per-word level `none` shows which word. It is the variant that adds the 5 extra golds.
  (6) Replay. The flat and layers candidates of the measurement are T10's records: no sentences, no per-word provenance, no flat P-4 flag; 12 of 12 (fast) live re-runs were identical (L-730); a full live sweep is not run. cross2 and s3000 are not run.
  (7) Effort and budgets. `effort` counts crosses per tier for the flat cross and WINDOWS for the windows; the search budgets differ (64 / 8 vs 512 / 64, L-705); the windows are read with representative members (L-715). A single node budget across the sources, or members "all", is not decided.
  (8) `--choose` / `--record` (the memory record of a chosen candidate) is not built for the combined list: what a chosen merged entry records (all its origins? the member the user clicked?) is not decided.
  (9) Layers: T10's stable-seats-path, variant A, compress is fixed (`--query-pass both` is accepted: A and B). Memory (corrected at review): the 19 GB probe was ONE call, not growth over a loop. 50 calls of ask_combined in one process on the toy corpus at fast stay at 52-54 MB resident (at fast / standard 52-58 MB; the stacks' read caches `_down` hold 5-34 entries and clear themselves above 4000). What explodes is matryoshka.ask_layered at effort `full` on the toy question 東京は何ですか (same on HEAD 1fbc76f2 without G3-g, also with the default `--layer-candidate path`): building an upper-layer cross, placement.build_cross takes its representative arrangement with `next(expand_flats(state[:1], L, twin_sets))` (placement.py, since T4d), and expand_flats feeds `itertools.permutations` of each twin set into `itertools.product`, which materialises every input before the first output: a twin set of 14 bundles = 14! (8.7e10) tuples (measured: 10 units already take 0.5 GB). Not a G3-g defect and not fixed here (placement.py is not a G3-g file); it is reachable from `vera line3 ask --effort full` with the layers on (the default), so it needs its own ticket. The layer stacks kept on the index (`_t8_stacks`) are bounded and not the cause.

## G3-g2 (2026-10-09): the combined list without merging across sources, in per-origin blocks, the typed abstentions first (verantyx/line3/combined.py `merge`, `also_in`, `header`, `blocks`; cli.py `--merge`; ask.py untouched, it passes `**kw`; tests/line3/test_combined.py; tests/line3/golden_combined_g3g.json.gz; experiments/line3/g3/combined/: summarize_g2.py, summarize_combined.py `merge="word_set"`, results/summary_g2.md, results/g2_win_*.jsonl)

### G3-g2 open points (owner questions; behaviour decided only as written above)
  (1) A single ANSWER now needs exactly one candidate in the whole list (L-744): the same word set from two origins is two entries and a CHOICE, where G3-g's merged list showed an ANSWER (the owner's 「全体の判定は今のまま」 applied to the entries as listed). On bank2 this never happens (0 verdicts change). Is that the intended reading, or should an agreement of origins on a lone word set stay a single answer (that would need a verdict that reads `also_in`, which the owner's "a mark only" forbids)?
  (2) Twin windows. Two windows of one origin with the same word set are two entries (L-700) and carry no `also_in` (the mark names OTHER origins): 5 / 22 such word sets at fast / standard. They are visible only as two entries of a block with the same words. A mark for them (`also_in` listing the origin itself, or a separate `twin_windows`) is not built.
  (3) Layers are ONE block (the owner lists six blocks): the layers' runs (tier, layer, variant) are in the source's order inside it; the origin of each entry names its run. A block per layer tier or per layer would make 3-9 blocks. The header also has one layers row, whose `kinds` count the runs that found nothing (55 / 60 of 94 questions at fast / standard list the layers and still have a run that ended without a fixed point).
  (4) The list got longer by the entries the merge had joined: 28.5 / 68 entries median (151 / 239 max), still dominated by flat and layers; the unmerged list makes the two window variants' equal sets two adjacent-block entries (25 / 58 word sets). The user's reading cost for a window gold is now 'go to the window block': the gold stands at position 1-2 (median 1) INSIDE its block, but the window blocks come last, at overall position up to 124 of 126. Block order (the owner chose it) is not a ranking, so no change was made; a collapsed / foldable display of the blocks that hold no gold is a product choice (summary_g2: a block lists something without gold in 6-54 of 69 questions).
  (5) The header says which source abstained but the verdict is CHOICE whenever any source lists (L-724 unchanged): 93 / 82 of 94 questions have at least one abstaining source, and the 25 unanswerable questions are 25 lists, none abstained (as G3-g). Whether a question on which the flat cross (or all three tiers) abstains while only window variants list should be marked more strongly than the header row is open (unans: flat/RUN lists 20 / 21 of 25, window/plain 7 / 9).
  (6) Text form: the header precedes the verdict line (「答え」 / 「候補 N 件」) for an ANSWER too; the 「答えなし（種類別）」 line was dropped as the header carries the counts. The `--format json` output has `header` and `blocks` in the answer.
  (7) Replay (as G3-g open point 6): flat and layers candidates in summary_g2 are T10's records (no sentences, no flat P-4 flag); the layers block order is the live order RUN, WORD, CHAR (T10 lists its tiers alphabetically). The window records were re-read and are identical to G3-g's.
  (8) (added at review) Block order. The owner chose 「出所ごとに区切って見せ、各区切りは安定の順」; the build keeps each block in its source's own order (L-743), which is word-set order for the flat tiers and window-then-word-set order for the windows, not an order by stability (bank2: flat/RUN blocks out of stability order in 61 / 78 and 71 / 82 questions with >= 2 entries). Either the owner confirms the source's own order, or each block is arranged by its own stability (most stable first, the source's order breaking ties: a stable sort inside the block, still no ranking across blocks); that changes the within-block positions of L-748 and the tests of Part 7, and needs the layers' stability, which T10's replayed records do not hold (replay.py gives the layers candidates no stability). Taken up in the G3-g2 addendum: L-749 arranges each block by its stability (layers replayed without stability stay order="source").

### G3-g2 addendum open points (owner questions)
  (1) The stability of a candidate is its source's own quantity: a layers block mixes runs of different tiers, layers and variants, so its stability order interleaves candidates whose stabilities came from different crosses (the owner asked for the order of the source; for the layers the "source's order" is run order, which L-749 replaces by the stability across runs). Sort the layers by run first and by stability inside a run instead?
  (2) Ties are kept in the source's order and are visible only as equal `stability` values; there is no tie-group field in the JSON and no tie mark in the text. 153 / 198 sorted blocks hold ties (flat/RUN 73 of 81 at fast): is a labelled tie group wanted?
  (3) The replay measurement cannot sort the layers block (T10's records carry no stability): the 11 / 24 layers golds stand at their source-order position (1-2 inside the block in both orders). A live re-run of the layers (an hour or more at 8 workers) would show whether the layers' stability order moves them.
  (4) Window candidates have stabilities that are strict-axis fractions of a window class; whether they are comparable to each other inside window/plain (different windows, different classes) is the owner's rule (「安定の順」) applied as written.

## G3-h (2026-10-09): the scope of the deeper z-edge count, `z_deep` "order_window", and the grid of the three pending "measure both" switches measured through the window-flat read (verantyx/line3/slide.py `WindowCounts.deep_z_window`, slide_place.py, slide_ratios.py; tests/line3/test_slide_place5.py; experiments/line3/g3/h/: build_caches.py, measure_h.py, cache_stats_h.py, summarize_h.py, results/summary.md, results/cache_stats.md)

This ticket builds (b)'s second reading and measures all three together with `z_deep` "slide", through the reading rule the owner chose after G3-e (「窓を平らな十字として読む」: slide_flat.py, G3-f; the combined list of G3-g2 sits on top of it and is not changed). Only the WINDOW rows of the combined list are measured (window/plain and window/window-evidence); the flat cross and the layers are unaffected by these switches. Three modules are extended (slide.py, slide_place.py, slide_ratios.py), docstrings of slide_query.py, one assertion of tests/line3/test_slide_query.py (`Q.Z_DEEPS`), one test file added; placement.py, ask.py, cli.py, slide_flat.py and the behaviour of slide_query.py are untouched (they take the value through `Z_DEEPS`). The default ("slide") and "order" are byte-identical (a digest computed with the committed code, below). Judgement points are numbered L-760.. (L-740..L-749 are G3-g2).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-760 | `z_deep` gets a third value, "order_window" (spec text `Z_DEEP_WINDOW_TEXT`, param `deep` = "order_window", so the slide spec sha and with it the place spec sha and the cache file name change; the default spec and "order" keep their bytes). The innermost z edge (the centre's neighbour) stays the slide edge, n_z. A DEEPER z edge (both ends are seats of the arm; L-661's positional definition, unchanged) carries the word order of its two units INSIDE the one sentence of the window both of its ends lie in (under growth z_reserved: the OTHER sentence, 「向こうの文」): `WindowCounts.deep_z_window(tier, arm, o, i, sid_o, sid_i)` = (n, omega, rows) with n = 1 when that sentence holds both units, else 0 (COUNT 1, not the corpus pair count of "order"), omega = 1 when the sentence shows the arm's direction (+z: o's first occurrence before i's; -z: after) else 0 ("direction only"), rows = the one x row of that sentence (before-row or after-row). The corpus is not counted: a pair that the corpus has in other sentences but the window's sentence does not is n 0. The scope of the counts (corpus | window) makes no difference: the sentence is a sentence of the window and both scopes hold its x row. | slide.WindowCounts.deep_z_window, Z_DEEPS, Z_DEEP_WINDOW_TEXT |
| L-761 | The sentence of an end. `WindowCounts.end_sid(tier, unit, sid)`: the seat's own `sid` when it has one (it must be a sentence of the window), else the unit's ONLY sentence of the window (`z_side`); a unit of both sentences with no sid of its own has none. The edge has evidence only when both ends name the same sentence (ends in different sentences, an end without a sentence, a unit outside the window, one unit twice: n 0, omega 0, no rows). Different sentences are possible only under a growth other than z_reserved or for a shared unit's second seat; there the edge is a plain "no evidence", NOT a fall-back to the corpus count. | slide.WindowCounts.end_sid |
| L-762 | Where a reader gets the sid. The placement and the verifier read the seat TOKEN (`slide_place.sid_of`: unit + SEP + sid for a unit of both sentences under seat_key unit_sid, else None, then L-761's z_side rule); the record writer reads the tokens of the two ends too (so the record states what the search weighed); slide_ratios reads the SeatRec's sid. Under the default seat_key unit_sid the three agree for every seat (a unit of one sentence has that sentence's sid, a shared unit has one seat per sentence). Under seat_key "unit" (the G3-c legacy, one seat per shared unit, not measured here) a shared unit's token carries no sid, so the placement gives every deeper edge that touches it no evidence while slide_ratios reads the seat's sid: the two can differ there. It is recorded, not guarded (no ValueError): the existing hash-seed tests build every seat_key. | slide_place.sid_of / ArmWeights.from_counts / _seat_rows, slide_ratios.counts_evidence |

The members need no per-edge rule (positional). `ArmWeights` keeps one deep function per rule: the weight of a deeper edge by arm code DEEP_Z + arm is (n, omega) of L-760 with the tokens' sids. | slide_place._edge_evidence / ArmWeights.from_counts, SlidePlacement.z_deep |

A test compares the two routes for every ordered pair, both arms and every sid combination of four toys (equal), and `cross_key`, `verify_class_slide`, `verify_fixed_point_slide` on toys under every growth / centre_scope / seat_key. | slide_place.window_order / counts_weight_fn |

### G3-h open points (owner; meaning level)
(1) The deeper-edge count of "order_window" gives n 1 to every deeper edge with both ends seated (1098 / 1098 budget, 755 / 755 x: under growth z_reserved both ends always lie in the other sentence, so n carries no information) and the direction (omega 1) to 98.9 / 98.8 %: with a z arm that holds one sentence the edge is a pure word-order edge, so it is not a "more evidence" or "less evidence" question but which of two readings of 「向こうの文」 the reader should use; the numbers above do not decide it. (2) The three rules' z keys are not comparable (G3-c4 open point 3 and G3-c3 open point 1 stay open, more pressing: the share of windows that keep both growths is 249 / 292 under order and 233 / 292 under order_window against 106 under slide at budget). (3) arm_cap x seats fewer units (65.9 / 73.2 / 73.2 % of the pairs' units against 67.2 / 78.8 / 77.7 % under budget) and leaves 351 / 486 / 455 units unseated by the cap (slide / order / order_window); the question runs above do not show a loss in the gold counts from this. (4) seat_empty_axis: since allow and deny seat the same units everywhere (above), the choice has no effect on any measured output; "deny" only records the denied arms. (5) Window-only single entries never ANSWER in the combined list (G3-g L-724); the single right / wrong columns are the flat grader's and are the lists of one entry there. (6) The sample is 69 + 25 questions of one corpus and the differences between cells are mostly 1 to 3 questions; no significance test was made. (7) `source_sids` does not cite the order_window rows (L-768).

### G3-j addendum (2026-10-10): the assembled strings are display only, they do not count in the verdict (verantyx/line3/combined.py `verdict_of`, `answer_obj`, `format_text`; tests/line3/test_combined.py; experiments/line3/g3/j/verdict_replay.py, results/verdict_replay.txt, results/measure_j.txt)

|---|---|---|

## G3-k (2026-10-10): the unknown-word stand-ins and the grammar layer's read order wired into the flat read, the layers, the windows and the combined list, `grammar="off"|"on"` (verantyx/line3/wiring.py [new]; grammar.py `stem`; cycle.py `QueryContext.standins`, `ReadPlan.grammar`, `plan_read(grammar=)`; ask.py; matryoshka.py `tier_kw`, `_variant_chain`; slide_query.py `Intake`; slide_flat.py `ask_flat(grammar=)`; combined.py; cli.py `--grammar on|off`; tests/line3/test_grammar_wiring.py; experiments/line3/g3/k/: measure_k.py, sweep_bank3.sh, sweep_bank2.sh, summarize_k.py, intake_survey.py, equiv_off.py, results/summary.md)

Binding from before: the grammar layer decides the READ ORDER only, never the candidate set (G2 4.2 / B-1, L-552); it reads the particle after the interrogative (slot), the predicate slot 「XのYは何ですか」 (L-548) and the question's granularity pattern with the stand-ins for unknown words (G2 OP-G2-7, L-550); 「語全体（WORD）の後ろの助詞を取る」 for a stem that ends inside a WORD (G2-f audit); the question is fed to every sovereign and sorted by FORM, 「両替機…タンク」 (G2-f audit); a stand-in is `granularity-derived`, not evidence of the unknown word (G1 I-G1-2) and a chance control is always reported (G1 3.2); the read order of windows is the question-unit count first and the grammar inside a tie (G3-e2, L-684). | id | decision | where |

The V3 adoption pools the end states of all crosses read by the number of sentences they share with the ORIGINAL units, so a new, higher-share state from a stand-in cross can displace older, lower-share entries: the list can lose entries as well as gain (never gain one from a cross that holds an original unit).
