### G3-k open points (owner; meaning level)
1. The stand-in semantics (L-802). Built: G1 L-G1-8 (1), the stand-ins select crosses and count in the read order, E_Q is the original units'. Not built: (2), one separate question per stand-in with the stand-in in the unknown word's place (the stand-in's section is then grounded). Evidence for (2): the stand-in units hold the gold string in 6 of 37 (bank3) and 14 of 45 (bank2) questions but the entries that exist only through a stand-in hold it in 0 of 5 and 1 of 5, because a stand-in cross is read with the unknown word's section ungrounded (it answers only through the question's other known words). Both alternatives to the built one were weighed: the stand-ins in the energies (tried, dropped, L-802: it swamped E_Q and the candidate set could not be filtered) and (2) (product of counts, up to 431 separate questions per word). Which one, and whether a cap on the stand-ins per word (OP-G1-7 (b) parts of 2+ characters, (c) stand-ins that share a sentence with another question word) is wanted.
2. The count-first order for the CROSSES (L-803) costs flat/RUN entries (9 of 38 questions under a quarter, uw02 with no stand-in at all; 修正 L-817: 4 of the 9 by the order alone (pa04 pa05 uw02 uw10) and part of pa10, 4 only once the stand-ins are added (uw09 uw08 uw15 pa19) and the rest of pa10) and helps nothing measurable alone (net 0 on bank3; +2 on bank2's flat block with 6 gained and 4 lost). The windows had it from G3-e2. Alternatives: the grammar kind first and E_Q inside it (G2 4.2 B-1 as first written), E_Q first and the count as a tie-break, splitting or reading a first block larger than the cap (G3-e open point 5).
3. The interrogative phrase of the question (何年, 何日, 何丁目, 最大何台, は何という) is an "unknown RUN word" by L-550 and G1's own count of 139; its stand-ins (the part 年: 119 units) are year strings, which is the half of the unit-level signal and 424 of the 2428 units. Whether the asked phrase gets stand-ins (it is not an unknown subject) is the owner's; excluding it is a one-line filter in `wiring.intake`, not built.
4. The layers' entries are not marked per entry (L-807): their provenance is a union over bundles; the layers' gold is 11 -> 18 on bank2 (their entries are unions of hundreds of words, which makes 'gold in a candidate' easy) and 5 -> 6 on bank3, through layer 0 being different (the stand-ins are not in their own reads, L-807). Marking them needs the bundle -> cross provenance.
5. The predicate form 「XのYは何ですか」 (50 of 94 bank2 questions, 16 of 38 bank3) has no particle to match (L-804), so the form tank changes nothing for it; the form is classified, reported and in the header row. OP-G2-7 (c) (an owner's choice) is what would give it an order.
6. `via_standin` marks entries all of whose states come from stand-in-only crosses; V3 pooling can also drop entries a stand-in state out-shares (修正 L-811: the stand-ins can also ADD entries from a cross with an original unit, through the tie-break under the cap, and through the V3 pool when the set of crosses read changes; see L-811 / L-818). A "grown" set measured against a stand-in-free baseline run (the order-only run is that baseline for bank3: 31 of 38 lists differ from it) is the stricter reading of 「候補は代役の印のついた単位を通してだけ増える」.
7. Only fast was measured. Under fast a stand-in-only cross is read only after every cross that holds an original unit (the key puts the originals first), so the stand-ins mostly act through the windows' second key; standard (10 crosses) is where a stand-in cross is read more often and was not run (a sweep of 38 takes about 1 h at fast, 3.5 times that at standard).
8. The stem rule is used only by the grammar-on records (L-801); the committed default records keep `straddle` (353 RUN stems), as G2-f's tests pin. Whether the default records change is the owner's.
9. The bank2 combined baseline of G3-g (29) used the z_deep-slide window placements; the clean off run of this tree gives 28 at fast (the recorded 29 stays the number of the earlier tables). (修正 L-817: the difference is G3-i's three changed defaults, z_deep order, seat_empty_axis deny and arm_cap budget, not z_deep only.) No fast baseline of the combined list with the G3-i defaults existed before this run.

## G3-k2 (2026-10-10): the flat plane's read order E_Q first (「E_Q が先、単位数は同点内」), both stand-in marks everywhere, the headline over the order-only run; L-819..L-825 (verantyx/line3/cycle.py `_plan_read_grammar`, `READ_ORDERS_FLAT`; wiring.py `ReadHook(order=)`, `flat_order_of`, `tier_kw` / `reask_kw` `order`; ask.py `ask(flat_order=)`, text form; combined.py `ask_combined(flat_order=)`, header counts; cli.py `--read-order eq_first`; tests/line3/test_grammar_wiring.py 33 tests; experiments/line3/g3/k/: measure_k.py `--flat-order`, sweep_k2.sh, summarize_k2.py, results/*_eq_first.*, summary_k2.md, summary.md)
Owner decisions (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, 「G3-k の測定後の決定」, verbatim choices): 平面の読む順 = 「E_Q が先、単位数は同点内」 (keep the existing energy order; only inside exact E_Q ties: original question units held -> stand-ins held -> grammar kind); 代役の印と見出し = 「両方の印を出し、見出しは順序のみ比」 (via_standin and read_via_standin both displayed; the stand-ins' effect reported as the gain over the order-only run). Defaults: grammar "off" is every committed byte (the goldens, `test_grammar_off_is_byte_identical_and_names_nothing`); with grammar "on" the flat order is now eq_first; G3-k's order stays as `qcount_first`. Not committed.

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-819 | The eq_first key. Per candidate cross of the cap read: `(group, -E_Q, -originals held, -stand-ins held, grammar rank)`, equal on every field = ONE block (never split, cap boundary and `partial` as before). "The existing energy order" is read as T7b's own order = the GROUP first (query_unit < holds_query_unit < shares_with_query), then E_Q descending; the group is not a "tie-break" key, so a cross whose seed is a stand-in unit stays in group query_unit (it is a marked query unit, L-802), exactly as in G3-k. E_Q is an integer count (`facts.n[seed] + sum npair(q, seed)` over the ORIGINAL units, the same formula as the off path), so "exact equality" is integer equality; no Fraction is needed and none is added. Consequences, stated rather than hidden: (i) over the same candidate set as G3-k (the crosses that hold an original unit or a stand-in) the cap read is T7b's order refined inside E_Q ties; (ii) the stand-in seeds' crosses (group query_unit, E_Q of the seed unit) are no longer pushed behind every original-holding cross (G3-k's key put "0 originals" last): see L-824. `ReadPlan.grammar` rows get a fifth field E_Q under eq_first (the qcount_first rows keep their four fields, so those bytes are G3-k's). `plan_read` docstring names both orders. | cycle._plan_read_grammar |
| L-820 | The switch. `ReadHook(tier, records, slot, order)`, `order` in `wiring.FLAT_ORDERS = ("eq_first", "qcount_first")`, default eq_first; `cycle._plan_read_grammar` reads `grammar.order` (a bare callable = eq_first). The order lives ON THE HOOK so the one object reaches (a) the main plan, (b) the `order_only_read` re-plan (cycle.ask_tier passes the same hook, so `read_via_standin` is the diff of the SAME ordering with and without the stand-ins), (c) the layers' re-asks (`reask_kw(..., order)`). Entrances: `ask(flat_order=None\|"eq_first"\|"qcount_first")`, `ask_combined(flat_order=)` (its `read_order` stays the WINDOWS' order qcount_first \| grammar_first, unchanged: windows have no E_Q), `vera line3 ask --read-order {eq_first,qcount_first,grammar_first}` with argparse default None: slide -> qcount_first as before (eq_first there is an error, exit 2); flat/combined with `--grammar on`: eq_first by default, `--read-order qcount_first` = the old behaviour (also names the windows' order qcount_first), `--read-order eq_first` = the windows' default qcount_first; `grammar_first` is a window order: error for flat, kept for the windows in combined (the flat plane keeps eq_first); with grammar off the option does nothing to the flat plane. The CLI help documents all of this. | wiring.py, ask.py, combined.py, cli.py |
| L-821 | Both marks wherever entries are printed. ### G3-k2 open points (owner; meaning level)
15. Under eq_first the stand-in seeds' crosses sort in group query_unit by E_Q, so many stand-in units (uw08 284, pa06 431) put many crosses early and the stand-ins' extra gold (G3-k +4/38 over the order alone) is gone: against the order-only run of the same order the stand-ins add 0 net on bank3 (+pa09 -uw19); the order alone brings 9 -> 10. Options: keep (the decision as built); put the stand-in seeds' crosses in group holds_query_unit (after the original units' crosses, E_Q-ordered); or keep qcount_first for the stand-in tie only. No code was changed on this.

Owner decision (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, 「G3-k2 の測定後の決定」, verbatim choice): 代役の種の十字の群 = 「代役の種は holds_query_unit の群へ (Recommended)」 — a stand-in is not "the question unit itself" but "a cross that holds a question unit"; the original words' crosses are always read first (group precedence); the E_Q-first order (L-819) is kept inside each group. This is open point 15 of G3-k2, option 2. Not committed.

This is the plan's reading (5.1: left_in_step = the rest of that step's candidates). Descendant: `descendants(old, new, step)` takes the units seated at `step` out of each new member (canon) and compares with the old members extended to the new L (`extend`); `frozen` = every new member projects onto an old member, `dropped` = the old members that no new member projects onto. `frozen` False raises StackError inside the step (a seated unit moved: a bug, never a result). ### G4-b measured

Tests: `tests/line3/test_stack.py` 83 tests, 83 passed at PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1 and 12345 (each ~80 s on the Pro under load). They cover: the prefix key against steps.py itself, step 0, refused input, the fold in process and across processes (build + save in a process with hash seed 0, load + extend in a process with seed 1, a single pass in a process with seed 12345; crosses, ledger and identity byte-equal; k = 1, 2, 3, foundation off and on), frozen seats (the descendant projection, the foundation seats keep their particle, `seated` / `left` only ever grow; a mutation that ignores `fixed` is caught), `_settle(fixed=)` itself on the placement toys, untouched crosses, birth = the one-shot build, the restricted fixed point, D-5 (the opening rule, every co-occurring unit seated or left and never both), closed crosses (at birth and while growing) stay closed, the ledger is complete (a line with sid evidence per seat change; every opened / grown / closed / rearranged cross named), foundation off / on, the CHAR-only stack with `fugashi` / `unidic_lite` blocked, the read view (an `ask.Index` over it answers a question and builds nothing on demand), save / load with refusals and a tampered file, workers 1 vs 2, no float. Toys: 8 sentences (4 documents) on CHAR / RUN / WORD, a 14-character sentence (every cross closes at birth), a 3-sentence set whose crosses close while growing, level `low`. Existing suites (foundation off, default paths): test_placement, test_placement_ordered, test_placement_skip, test_foundation, test_variants, test_g4_steps, test_slide_place (but the byte pin, L-G4-52) all pass with the `fixed=` change; `test_carry_tower.py::test_default_pack_overflow_is_close_and_byte_identical_to_head[RUN|WORD]` fails the same way in wt/line3 at HEAD without this change (its pinned shas predate the first-class rule), so it is not caused here.

Real data (the first 6 articles, RUN, foundation on, mid, 2 workers; a check script, not a committed test): the single-pass state at step 6 and `load(step 5)` + `extend(article 6)` in another process (hash seed 1) have the same bytes (T-G4-4 on fulllead for k = 5); `verify_cross` passed for the 3 crosses keyed at step 6 with at most 60 members (the other 44 were skipped as too big to re-check), and 3 of 3 small births equal `build_cross` of the prefix.

Per-document cost, the first 8 articles of fulllead (20 sentences; `experiments/line3/g4/stack_timing.py`, RUN, level mid, foundation ON, 2 workers, PYTHONHASHSEED 0, Python 3.11, the Pro with load1 62 at the start and 29 at the end, so the seconds are inflated by other jobs; `results/stack_timing_8.txt`): 274.5 s wall, 191.8 s CPU in all = 34.3 s wall / 24.0 s CPU per document, 13.7 s wall / 9.6 s CPU per sentence. Per step (sentences / new units / wall s / CPU s / crosses closed at the end of the step of the prefix's crosses): 1: 3 / 24 / 29.5 / 22.7 / 21 of 24; 2: 3 / 20 / 3.7 / 3.1 / 22 of 44; 3: 6 / 66 / 101.2 / 70.8 / 83 of 110; 4: 1 / 9 / 20.6 / 11.9 / 84 of 119; 5: 1 / 5 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 84 of 124; 6: 3 / 45 / 113.3 / 78.1 / 123 of 169; 7: 1 / 8 / 2.6 / 2.1 / 131 of 177; 8: 2 / 8 / 3.4 / 2.8 / 137 of 185. The cost is carried by the births (a new unit's one-shot build, quotient off): 66 births = 101 s, 45 births = 113 s, 9 births = 21 s, a document with only a few new units costs seconds. Growth happened once (step 6: 2 crosses grown, 17 units seated into empty seats, 1 narrowed, 78 of 720 members dropped in one of them, L 3 -> 4); at the other seven steps no open cross had a new co-occurring unit. Diagnostic, foundation OFF (same settings, load1 28 -> 22): 317.1 s wall, 343.5 s CPU = 39.6 s / 42.9 s per document, 129 of 185 crosses closed; growth at step 3 (1 cross, 9 fills, 1 narrowed), 6 (2, 10, 1) and 8 (2, 10, 2). state_sha256 (RUN, step 8): ON 8c0415f8ce2b642116a3af6c25dedd14b4b4acd19d019a3356c01efd64d26b59, OFF c481a58590c4d3f88166c7ce24f3cf3835fc0912765fad80706a684c6d2d89a5.

Reading for the plan's estimate (8): at 9.6 CPU s per sentence (RUN, ON) a full 592-sentence RUN pass would be about 5,700 CPU s if the per-sentence cost stayed what it is at 20 sentences, which it will not exactly (a bigger prefix has more open crosses to grow, but 74 % of the crosses are already closed at 8 articles and closed crosses cost nothing); the one-shot F1 build of RUN costs 3,281 s OFF (about 3,900 s ON, G1-b) and the births of a stack pass are of that order, so a RUN pass of the order of one one-shot build (1-2x) is the figure this sample supports, a lower bound for the growth part. This is a 20-sentence sample, not a measurement of 592.

### G4-b open points (reviewer / owner)
1. The closure share is the plan's "largest risk" and it is already visible at article 1: with the foundation ON 21 of 24 RUN crosses close at birth by the budget (mid), 137 of 185 after 8 articles (74 %); with the foundation OFF it is 129 of 185 (70 %). So quotient off alone (L-G4-25) closes most crosses; the foundation adds to it (14 vs 21 of 24 at step 1). A closed cross only records new co-occurring units, so gold that arrives later than the closing step can only ever reach the cross through `left_after`. Gate G-2 (L-G4-32) must read this; no threshold was applied here.
2. `fixed=` is in placement.py (L-G4-52), so `test_slide_place.py::test_nothing_is_hooked_and_placement_py_is_unmodified` fails until the commit that holds this change.
3. The plan underdetermined the `left` fields (L-G4-55): "the rest of that step's candidates" was read as the whole rest of the step's candidate list (also later share-groups), unlike the placement's group-based `left_in_group` / `left_after`; the view maps them to those names (counts only).
4. The plan's delta snapshots (L-G4-26) became full snapshots (L-G4-26 changed); at full scale a RUN snapshot is large (classes of up to 1000 flats of 19-37 seats per cross). A content-addressed store that writes each cross version once would keep any identity and make the 66 saved steps affordable; not built.
5. A cross whose seed is in the document and has nothing new to seat is not re-keyed (L-G4-54): its `key` can be older than the counts of the prefix, and the view recomputes `score` / `a_num` on the prefix for display; the members of a class that has not changed since `keyed_at` need not tie under the newer counts. The reader selects by neither.
6. The old class can lose members through the RECOUNT alone (a member whose key fell behind once the document's sentences were counted), not only through the new units: `dropped` counts both (the plan's 絞り is "a member with no descendant" and does not separate them). The ledger cannot tell them apart; a split needs the keys of the old members under the new counts (cheap to add).
7. Not done (other tickets / forbidden files): the CLI `line3 stack build` (cli.py), `Index.from_stack`, `_Store(on_demand=False)`, refusing `effort="full"` and `build_space(tiers=)` (G4-c; the stack's own `_build_space` builds the CHAR-only space, L-G4-61), the 8 T10 records and the C arm (G4-e), cross-machine identities (T-G4-12; the Python 3.13 / GHA values are not computed here).
8. The 8-article timing is one run on a loaded machine (no repeat).

The 8-article RUN state sha is `8c0415f8ce2b6421` (unchanged by L-G4-69 and L-G4-70: the split only adds ledger fields, and the toy-less case of L-G4-69 is not met in those 8 articles).

### G4-b after review: open points
1. The meaning of 絞り (R / U / A) is for the owner; L-G4-70 only measures how much of it the recount alone explains (on the 8 articles: none). If the owner wants the recount not to count as 絞り, `dropped` would have to become `dropped_new`; not done.
2. The on-demand guard for a stack cache (L-G4-68) is G4-c: until it exists `ask_tier` with its default `raise_budget` bypasses the stack for every closed cross of a view. `from_stack` is the flag to test; it is not serialised.
3. `dropped_recount` is a key comparison before seating, not a proof of cause (L-G4-70): a member below the best key could in principle have produced a best-total arrangement; the 8 articles and the toys show the classification as defined, not its limit.
4. The size estimate of L-G4-71 is an extrapolation from one tier and 8 articles; the closure share and class sizes at 300 articles are not known. The ledger-per-snapshot duplication is the part that a cheap change (append-only ledger) removes; not done, no redesign asked.
5. The mutation test leaves two blind spots by design (MANY, GROW on, L-G4-66); a toy that grows an open cross with the foundation on and fills it would close the second; not built.

### G4-c open points (reviewer / owner)

1. `effort=None` is not refused on a stack (L-G4-80): it reads whole, the guard refuses the rebuilds and records them. If the owner wants a stack to take only fast / standard / nodes, `ask` needs one more line (`name is None` besides `"full"`). (Decided by the owner: effort None stays allowed, only `full` is refused; pinned by L-G4-100.)
2. `read.partial` is true for a stack when a closed cross was not rebuilt, besides the cap (L-G4-76); `partial_reasons` tells which. Everywhere else `partial` is still "unread by the cap". Whether a closed cross that was read and gave no state should count as partial is a meaning question (the cross is at its capacity, N-05: a rebuild could give it more, which the frozen stack does not do). (修正 L-G4-95: built the other way now: `partial` stays the cap's; the refusal is in `rebuild_refused` and `partial_reasons`. The owner is asked to confirm this reading.)
3. `Index.from_stack` builds the prefix space twice (its own `build_space(rows, tiers=)`, and the stack's memo for `as_placements` and the adhesion): fine at 8 articles (0.4-2.2 s), a cost at 300 (592 sentences, the records for RUN / WORD); one shared space would need `stack.py` to take a space (not edited here).
4. The first ask on an index pays the grammar context once (`wiring.context_of`: span index + particle records of the prefix); the per-question times above include it in the first row of each index only.
5. The relation labels (L-G4-81) are the union over the tied arrangements that the contraction merges, so a word often lists several particles (が・で・に); a per-arrangement display, or only the labels common to all of them, would be a design choice.
6. A foundation-off stack and a foundation-on stack are two sub-directories of one root; `--foundation` selects it. A snapshot written with another `--level` or `--order` is refused, not guessed.
7. `Index.stack_state` keeps the whole `StackState` (all documents and ledgers) alive with the index; harmless at 8 articles, to be dropped by a caller that reads many steps in one process.
8. The smoke run is 20 sentences: it shows the plumbing (the same entries as the one-shot build at step 1, the guard, the step identity, the times), and that at 8 articles no gold of the three intra2 questions is listed; it is not what the meter will measure at 66 steps.

### G4-c review fixes: tests and runs

`tests/line3/test_g4c_read.py` 43 tests (was 30), `test_stack.py` 111, `test_ask.py` 26 (each run alone), `test_combined.py` 54 at hash seeds 0 / 1 / 12345, `tools/determinism_probe.py` unchanged (79b0a11f444ec220 / a44611defdd6bec4 / 51b97f502940dcc2). The foundation-off goldens (`golden_g4c_off.json`) are unchanged.

### Open points after the review fixes

1. `partial_reasons` can be non-empty while `partial` is false (the stack reason at effort None). That follows the owner's reading (partial = the cap only; the refusal in `partial_reasons` / `rebuild_refused`); a reader who tests `partial_reasons` alone to decide "incomplete" must also read `rebuild_refused`.
2. The layers' `bundle_builds` counts the builds of the question asked, not of the cached layer-1 "same" layer; a meter that wants the total cost must read it on a fresh index.
3. A foundation-on stack's layers build their bundle crosses with the foundation OFF (unchanged behaviour); the mark says "outside the stack", not "seated".

### G4-d open points (reviewer / owner)
1. **Reading of the closure**: most crosses close at birth in WORD and CHAR (73.7 % / 72.7 % of all crosses; 78-80 % closed) and a slim majority in RUN (54.9 % at birth, 58.0 % closed); overall 93.9 % of the closures are at birth, so a closed cross is almost always closed before any later document can reach it, and after that a later co-occurring unit can only be recorded. And independently of the closure, growth is rare because 89 % of the RUN seeds (76 % WORD) occur in one article only. The numbers do not say whether this "measures the budget instead of growth" (the plan's largest risk); they show that the measured growth lives in about 570 crosses (6.6 %). Whether that is enough for the meter, and whether L-G4-32 should be read on these numbers, is the owner's.
2. L-G4-32 (per intra2 question) is not computed, see L-G4-95. It is the actual gate; it needs the question-unit and gold-unit mapping of bank2 and the saved snapshots, no rebuild.
3. "Frozen share" was not defined by the plan; the two definitions of L-G4-88 are mine. The jsonl has the raw counts to recompute any other.
4. The share of narrowing caused by the recount alone is large at scale (27 / 43 / 47 % of the dropped members, L-G4-93) while the 8-article sample showed none. The owner's question on whether the recount should count as 絞り (G4-b open point 1) now has numbers behind it.
5. The timings are from a loaded machine (see L-G4-94) and one pass; the CPU seconds are inflated by an unknown factor (step 1: 117 s against 27 s wall in a calibration run), the shares are not affected (the state is byte-identical for any load and worker count, L-G4-63).
6. The fold check at k = 13, 34 compares a three-tier build from the prefix file with the snapshot; `--resume` of `build` was exercised on a small run only. The 8-article B check does not cover steps beyond 8 (L-G4-90).
7. No code outside `experiments/line3/g4/gate2_build.py` and `results/` changed; nothing was committed. stack.py needed no change to run at scale (2.7 GB RSS, 3.2 CPU h).

## G4-d2（門 G-2 の問いごとの判定）(2026-10-11)

Ticket: docs/LINE3_G4_GROWTH_METER.md 9 ticket 7, criterion L-G4-32 (open since L-G4-95): for each of the 69 intra2 questions, from the SAVED stack snapshots of arm A (`/Users/motonisihikoudai/Projects/vera-impl/cache/g4_stack_A/found-a2083d453637__mid__forward`, 59 steps x 3 tiers: the 58 distinct entry steps and 300), no rebuild, nothing run through the reader. New: `experiments/line3/g4/gate2_question.py` (one sub-command `run`, one process, no clock), `results/gate2_question.md`, `results/gate2_question.jsonl` (414 records = 69 questions x {e(q), 300} x 3 tiers). Nothing else changed; nothing committed. The worktree `line3-g4d2` (branch `line3-g4d2` from line3 5bf50536).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-G4-110 | The reading of the criterion, mechanical. Units of the space = the keys of `state.crosses[tier]` (stack.as_placements asserts that they are exactly the tier's units; checked here too: the units of the step-55 snapshot equal the units of the first 55 articles' sentences in a whole-corpus space). Question units per tier = `cycle.split_question(tier, q)` minus `funcwords.default_filter(tier)` (exactly what `ask_tier` does with the grammar off), deduplicated; "present" = a unit of the space. Gold units = every unit of the space for which the T9 scorer rule holds (`scorer.hits_words`: a normalised gold alternative is a substring of the normalised text of ONE unit), plus a flag for those whose normalised text equals an alternative. A cross "holds" a unit if it is its seed or a seated unit (the V1 rule of `plan_read` / `placement_units`; checked: for every cross at steps 55 and 144 the data units of every member equal the seated units, 7570 crosses, 0 mismatches). Every state identity was recomputed from the raw canonical bytes while loading (a light loader that keeps only seed, opened_at, closed_at, seated, left). | gate2_question.py |
| L-G4-111 | The verdict per (question, step, tier), in this order. 未着: no unit spells a gold alternative. reachable: a gold unit is seated in some cross that holds a question unit (the gold's own cross is such a cross whenever it holds a question unit; both routes are reported). closed-before: not reachable, at least one question unit in the space, and EVERY question-unit cross is closed at a step strictly before e(q) (the entry step of the gold's article; the maximum step of the evidence articles equals e(q) for all 69, asserted). other, with a sub-tag: `closed_at_entry` (every question-unit cross is closed, one of them AT e(q) or later), `open_no_cooccurrence` (a question-unit cross is open and the gold sits in no holding cross), `no_question_unit`. The same pair of numbers is also kept per question-unit cross: open / closed, opened_at, closed_at, at birth (closed_at == opened_at), size, whether a gold unit is seated in it, and `cooccur` = how a gold unit stands to it in its own ledger of the cross (seated | left_in_step | left_after | none; a cross records every unit that shares a sentence with its seed). | gate2_question.py |
| L-G4-112 | MEASURED (entry and step 300 give the same verdict for every one of the 69 questions in every tier). RUN: reachable 40, closed-before 0, 未着 19, other 10 (closed_at_entry 3: I2-020, R2-I007, R2-I012; open_no_cooccurrence 7: I2-011, I2-039, I2-043, R2-I002, R2-I003, R2-I004, R2-I019). WORD: 17 / 0 / 51 / 1 (open_no_cooccurrence: I2-011). CHAR: 1 / 0 / 68 / 0 (I2-025, gold the one character 青). Across tiers (a question once): reachable in some tier 41, 未着 in every tier 18, other 10, blocked by closure 0. **The stop condition of L-G4-32 is not met: 0 of 69 questions are closed-before in any tier, at e(q) or at 300** (widened to "at or before the gold article's own step": 3 of 69 = 4.3 % in RUN, 0 in WORD and CHAR). | results/gate2_question.md |
| L-G4-113 | Why the strict criterion cannot fire as worded (for the reader of L-G4-112). Every question that has a gold unit also has a question unit whose cross was OPENED at e(q) (50 of 50 in RUN, 18 of 18 in WORD, 1 of 1 in CHAR): the subject of an intra2 question is the title of the article that holds the gold, so it is new in the article of the gold. A cross opened at e(q) cannot have closed before e(q). The failure the criterion is after shows up as closure AT birth instead, and it is counted separately: in RUN 11 of 50 questions with a gold unit, in WORD 16 of 18, in CHAR 1 of 1 have a closed question-unit cross that recorded a gold unit as left (the gold shares a sentence with the seed, the cross was closed and did not seat it); every one of those 28 is still reachable through another holding cross. Reachable with NO question-unit cross seating the gold: RUN 9, WORD 7, CHAR 1 (the gold is reached through the gold's own cross or a third cross). | results/gate2_question.md |
| L-G4-114 | Closure AT BIRTH among the question-unit crosses (distinct crosses; a unit asked by several questions once). At e(q): RUN 79 of 181 (43.6 %; closed 86, 47.5 %), WORD 221 of 342 (64.6 %; closed 79.5 %), CHAR 610 of 724 (84.3 %; closed 92.1 %). At 300: RUN 80 of 183 (43.7 %; closed 51.4 %), WORD 190 of 287 (66.2 %; closed 80.5 %), CHAR 300 of 365 (82.2 %; closed 92.6 %). Against all crosses of the tier at 300 (L-G4-92): RUN 54.9 %, WORD 73.7 %, CHAR 72.7 % at birth. So the question-unit crosses close at birth less often than the average cross in RUN and WORD (question words are the content units of the article) and more often in CHAR (a question cut into characters uses the common ones). | results/gate2_question.md |
| L-G4-115 | The 未着 rows, and why they are mostly the tokeniser. RUN 19, WORD 51, CHAR 68 questions have no unit that spells a gold alternative. For 15 of the 19 (RUN), 42 of 51 (WORD) and 60 of 68 (CHAR) the gold alternative IS spelled by adjacent kept units of the evidence sentence (the tier cut it, e.g. ハッシュ表 into ハッシュ + 表 in both RUN and WORD, so no unit spells it): the §7.4 clause "and no path spells it" is therefore not applied here (see open point 2), and these are counted 未着 on the unit rule the task named. 4 / 9 / 8 are not even spelled by the concatenation of the kept units (the gold holds a dropped function unit or a character the tier does not keep). In RUN every reachable question is reachable through a gold unit that sits in the evidence sentence itself (40 of 40), WORD 17 of 17: no reach is spurious. | results/gate2_question.md |

### G4-d2 verification
`PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and `1` give byte-identical `gate2_question.jsonl` (a65585453414cdff0bb8e3c4185c983f); the md differs only by the optional `--selfcheck` lines. The script reads `bank2.tsv`, `steps.json`, the snapshots and `fulllead_sents.jsonl`; `vera-impl/hidden` is not opened. The grammar-off question cut was not run through `ask`; it calls the same `split_question` and `default_filter`.

### G4-d2 open points (reviewer / owner)
1. **The strict wording cannot fire for this bank** (L-G4-113): the gate is passed vacuously on "closed before the article entered". If the intent is "closed without the gold seated although it co-occurs", the measure to read is the `cooccur` field: gold left in a closed question-unit cross in 11 of 50 (RUN), 16 of 18 (WORD) questions with a gold unit, all still reachable by another route. Owner: keep L-G4-32 as worded, or restate it on `cooccur`.
2. **未着 uses the unit rule only.** The 69 questions do not say whether "a path spells it" (§7.4) counts a gold cut into adjacent units; if it does, the RUN 未着 falls from 19 to 4, WORD from 51 to 9, CHAR from 68 to 8 (L-G4-115), and those 15 / 42 / 60 questions move into the reader's miss column instead of the excluded column.
3. **The sentence-level co-occurrence is the stack's.** A gold unit in the SAME article but in another sentence than the question's units never co-occurs with their seeds (I2-001: ハッシュ表 sits in a sentence without ハッシュテーブル). `cooccur: none` is then not a closure effect. 7 of the 10 RUN "other" rows are open crosses for that reason.
4. **Reachable is not read.** It says the gold is seated where the reader's V1 rule would look; whether the entry is formed, ranked inside the cap, or adopted is for the meter (G4-e). The route fields (`reach_via`, `reach_evidence_unit`) are in the jsonl.
5. The CHAR tier is 未着 for every multi-character gold on the unit rule (68 of 69); its closed-at-birth share is reported but the CHAR verdicts carry no information on the gate.

Design decisions implemented as written (L-LOOM-01 .. L-LOOM-23 of docs/LINE3_LOOM_DESIGN.md 12.3; the ones marked "later" belong to tickets not in the core):

| id | decision | where |

### LOOM-core open points
1. `foundation.a_num` adds the CENTRE word's は adhesion to `a` whether or not the cross is marked `topic` (the key is topic-blind). The gate uses `placement.seated_key` as it is (the owner's OP-LOOM-1 wording), so a cross whose centre word has は evidence is judged with that evidence even without the topic mark. Reported, not changed (foundation.py is not touched). RESOLVED by the owner's OP-LOOM-4 「主題の印があるときだけ数える」: see L-LOOM-51 (the first sentence above describes the first build).
2. The gate judges a cross one swap at a time (a fixed point of the single-swap moves of `verify_class_foundation`), exactly as the design says; the named swap is an improving step, and a refused cross may need more than one swap. `best_swaps` can hold several swaps; the loom never picks one.
3. CODE is not emit-capable until LOOM-e (L-LOOM-36). `tasks_bank2.jsonl`, `score.py`, the harness CLI of 9.4, the windows, the loops, the L2 driver and the L1 files (`.mcp.json`, agent definitions) are later tickets; `vera loom output` is the minimal L4 consumer so that "free text scores nothing" is testable now.
4. `vera loom replay` of a folder that does not exist exits 1 (DIFFERS: unreadable), not 2; cosmetic.
5. A tool call whose arguments violate the tool's JSON schema is rejected by the MCP SDK before `LoomServer.call` and leaves no ledger row (such a call can neither change the state nor produce output); this is now an explicit decision with a stated boundary, L-LOOM-46. If every attempt must be a row, the tool parameters would have to be typed loosely and validated by `_args`; that costs the model its schema.
6. The corpus build (about 0.6 s) happens at the first `begin` of a process, not at server start.
7. Everything is labelled with the owner's recommended defaults, which the owner has now confirmed (OP-LOOM-1 (a), OP-LOOM-2 (a), OP-LOOM-3 (a)); nothing was run on a model (no meter, no LLM, no network).

## LOOM-core（審査後の修正）(2026-10-11): the review of the loom core (Opus: merge after fixes) applied, plus the owner's OP-LOOM-4

Files touched: verantyx/loom/{ledger,ops,state,read,mcp}.py, verantyx/cli.py (the `demo` task ids), tests/line3/test_loom_review.py [new, 26 tests], test_loom_stability.py (+4), test_loom_ledger.py and test_loom_mcp.py (one assertion / one docstring each). verantyx/line3/*.py NOT touched (`foundation.a_num` and `placement.seated_key` keep their bytes; OP-LOOM-4 is a loom-local variant). Earlier L text was corrected in place with 「(修正 L-LOOM-4x)」 notes (L-LOOM-19, 24, 29, 28, 31, 32, 33, 41, the owner-decisions paragraph, the test line, open points 1 and 5).

| id | decision | where |
|---|---|---|
| L-LOOM-43 | `verify` and `replay` judge the BYTES of ops.jsonl, not a parsed copy. `verify_chain` splits the raw bytes and requires every line to equal `canonical(row)` (UTF-8) exactly, else `NONCANONICAL_LINE` (status TAMPERED); this catches inserted whitespace, key order, an escaped character, and a duplicate key (the parser keeps the LAST of two equal keys, so a prepended or appended `"result"` hashed as the real one and could be output). `replay` compares `line_of(row)` to the raw line + newline after the dict comparison; the same dict in other bytes is `DIFFERS` with field `bytes` (an unterminated last line too). `emitted_output` therefore refuses (`run_not_verified`) for all of them, in code and in `vera loom output`. Tests: whitespace insertion, 4 other spellings, prepended and appended duplicate-key forgery (+ the CLI), replay field `bytes` | ledger.verify_chain, ledger.replay, test_loom_review |
| L-LOOM-44 | What a call may cost the ledger (design 7.4 bounds the lookup strings at 30 x 32 chars and calls "refused calls recorded anyway", but the first build stored the arguments of EVERY call verbatim: 200 refused `abstain` x 4,000 chars = 4.9 MB with verify OK; after `run_closed` every call was stored verbatim too). Now: (a) the arguments of a model call are stored verbatim only while their canonical JSON is at most `ARGS_CHARS_CAP` = 512 chars and no string (value or key) exceeds `ARG_STR_CAP` = 64 (the design's unit sizes are lookup 32, constructed 8 / 40, model id 64; every legitimate call is far below); otherwise the row has `"args":{}`, `"truncated":true`, `"args_sha256"`, `"args_chars"` and the call is refused `args_too_large` (it still counts in its class, like `secret_shaped_unit`; oversize wins over the secret scan, so nothing of the arguments is stored). (b) Two guard counters, in the state (`state.guards`, in `state_sha`, shown by `status`), caps `abstain_refused` 5 and `closed_calls` 20: every refused `abstain` counts in the first, every model call after the close in the second; beyond the cap the call is refused `cap_exceeded {guard, limit}` and stored as sha256 + length only. A VALID abstain is never blocked, so the model can always close its run. (c) `begin`: at most `max_begins` = 256 successful begins per server process, then `cap_exceeded {guard: "begin"}`; a refused begin has no run and therefore no ledger, so nothing is stored (there is no sha + length to keep). (d) A result never echoes more than 64 chars of an argument (`abstain` bad_type: 32; `unknown_task`: 64). Measured: 200 refused abstains x 4,000 chars now < 120 KB (was 4.9 MB), 300 closed-run calls x 4,000 chars < 250 KB. HONEST RESIDUE of design 7.4: the NUMBER of calls is still not bounded for `status` (uncapped by design), for calls refused by a class cap (`ops_cap`, `lookup_cap`, ...) and for harness rows; each is now at most ~1 KB (512 chars of arguments + its result), so growth is linear in the number of calls instead of in their size. A per-run total-row cap would close it (open point 2). The values 64 / 512 / 5 / 20 / 256 are this build's defaults, not the owner's | ops._oversize, ops.Run._model_step / _guard_blocked, state.GUARD_CAPS, mcp.LoomServer.begin |
| L-LOOM-45 | Run ids over MCP are unguessable (this corrects L-LOOM-24): `mcp.build` sets `LoomServer.nonce = os.urandom(16).hex()`, mixed into the id hash; so the formula (task, model, corpus_sha, seq from 0) that any weaver could compute no longer names another weaver's run (`status` / `emit` / `abstain` on it are `unknown_run`; another server's run is not reachable either). `nonce=None` (the default of `LoomServer`) keeps the exact old formula, tested byte for byte, so scripted runs and the cross-seed byte identity are unchanged. A replay reads the id from row 0 and never derives it: a run made under one nonce replays byte-identically, and a server restarted with another nonce reloads it | mcp.LoomServer._derive_run_id, mcp.build |
| L-LOOM-46 | The boundary of "one call = one row". EVERY call that reaches `LoomServer.call` with one of the 18 tools and the id of an existing run appends exactly one row to that run's ledger (tested over all 17 non-begin tools with empty and with unknown arguments). ### LOOM-core review fixes: open points
1. The は-adhesion point (open point 1 of the first build) is closed by OP-LOOM-4 (L-LOOM-51).
2. The number of calls is still unbounded for `status`, for calls refused by a class cap, and for harness rows (L-LOOM-44, honest residue); a per-run total-row cap (for example 600 model rows) would bound the ledger by rows x ~1 KB. Not built; owner's call.
3. L-LOOM-47 makes every Python patch upgrade a `python_mismatch` for ALL recorded runs, not only code runs. If the owner wants prose runs to survive a patch upgrade, the key could depend on the run's lang (prose: MAJOR.MINOR; code: full); not built.
4. `max_begins` is per server process (a restart resets it) and counts successful begins; the real bound on disk is the runs directory, which the operator owns.
5. `unknown_tool` with an existing run leaves no row (L-LOOM-46 (iii)); if the owner wants those recorded, the op would have to be stored as a sha256 + length.
6. The caps of L-LOOM-44 (64 / 512 / 5 / 20 / 256) are this build's defaults.

| L-LOOM-70 | The CODE record index (completes L-LOOM-11). `CodeIndex` is built from `{relpath: bytes}` that the CALLER read (code.py opens no file: T-LOOM-32); `fixture.py` lists and reads through a `reader` (the server's `Sandbox.read_bytes`, a replay's `loader`), so every file is sandbox-checked. Files: every `*.py` under the fixture root, sorted by relative path, EXCEPT `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `__pycache__` and dot-folders (a test file names the function the task asks for; an index that holds the answer's names is not a corpus). Tokens: NAME / OP / NUMBER / STRING (keywords are NAMEs); each occurrence is `(path, line, col)`, line 1-based, col 0-based as `tokenize` gives it; a token that spans lines (a triple-quoted string) is not a unit. A "sentence" is one logical line (NEWLINE to NEWLINE), `source` = `path:line` of its first token, `text` = its source lines joined by one space (≤ 200 chars), sids in (path, line) order. Definitions: `def` / `class` / assignment, `for` / augmented / annotated targets, import aliases, each with `scope` (`<module>`, `Counter`, `Counter.bump`, ...); parameters are not indexed. `index.sha` = sha256 of the canonical `{v: "code_index.v1", files: {path: sha256(bytes)}}`; it is `header.code_index_sha` and `replay` compares it (`code_index_sha_mismatch`, which `header_mismatch` already had). A file that does not tokenize / parse is a `ValueError` (`begin` -> `fixture_unreadable`); a link out of the fixture is `path_outside_sandbox` for the whole `begin`; a replay with no `fixture` in `meta.json` is the INPUTS status `fixture_unresolved` (also `fixture_outside_sandbox`, `fixture_unreadable`). `lookup(text, CODE\|any)` -> `{tier, surface, n, occ (the first 8 [path, line, col]), sids (the first 20 distinct), sentences (the first 5 {sid, source, text})}` (n is complete; the lists are bounded so a row for `(` stays small); `read_sentence(sid)` -> `{sid, source, text, units: {CODE: [tokens]}}`; `add record tier=CODE` -> a unit with `prov = {tier, n, occ (first 8), files: {path: sha256}}` (so `read._unit_seg` and the display need no change). | code.CodeIndex, fixture.py, ops.h_lookup / h_read_sentence / h_add, mcp.begin, ledger.replay |
| L-LOOM-71 | Definition-first as built (completes L-LOOM-12). At `read` / `emit`, after the parse gate passes, one AST walk in source order with a scope stack: a `Name` in Load context must be bound EARLIER in the text, in the same or an enclosing scope, or be a builtin, or be a CONTEXT name. Binders: `def` (bound before its body, so recursion works; the defaults are read in the enclosing scope first), parameters (function scope), assignment targets (the value is read BEFORE the targets are bound: `x = x + 1` with no `x` is refused), `for` targets, import aliases, the one comprehension form's variables (the comprehension scope; they do not leak). A function body that names a LATER module-level def is refused (the rule is "seated earlier", K4). Context names = the task's `context_names` (explicit) plus the top-level names of `target.file` (the emitted text is appended at the END of the target file, so all of them are earlier); a name that lives in ANOTHER fixture module is not a context name and needs its import cross earlier in the thread (K3). Builtins = `code.BUILTINS`, a tuple embedded in code.py (CPython 3.11 `sorted(dir(builtins))` minus the names `site` adds: copyright credits exit help license quit), pinned by a test against `dir(builtins)` on 3.11 (the design's separate `builtins_py311.txt` was not made: code.py cannot read a file). A constructed NAME therefore needs a definition cross (def, assignment, import, `for`) earlier in the same thread. Refusal: `undefined_name {name, line, col, cid, defined_in}`; `defined_in` lists up to 3 `path:line` of a non-import module-level definition of that name in the fixture (the hint that an import is missing). The gate runs only on a tree WITHOUT unsupported constructs (a name in a tree the loom does not read is not judged). | code._DefinitionFirst, read.evaluate |

Imports: `import m` / `from m import a` is allowed when m is a module of the fixture (`calc`, `calc.ops`, ... from the index paths) and, for `from`, `a` is a module-level name of m or a submodule `m.a`; or m is in the pinned stdlib list (`math itertools functools collections re json fractions typing dataclasses operator string`); else `import_not_allowed {module, name?, line, reason: module\|name\|relative}`. A relative import is refused (`relative`). A refused import still binds its names (one refusal, no cascade of `undefined_name`). Unsupported constructs: the design's L-LOOM-13 is a blocklist (global nonlocal del star-import eval exec compile __import__ open getattr setattr); the owner's ticket asks for the smallest subset. Both are implemented: an ALLOW-LIST of statements `def return assign call-statement if for import from-import` and of expressions (names, constants, calls, unary / binary / boolean / comparison operators, attributes, subscripts, tuples, lists, ONE comprehension form: a list comprehension with `for` / `if` clauses, which K5 needs), and the blocklisted calls inside it [修正 L-LOOM-78: the blocked NAMES, read or called, and dunder names / attributes]. Everything else is `unsupported_construct {construct, line, cid}` with the AST class name (`ClassDef AsyncFunctionDef Lambda While Try With Global Delete Match Yield Await Dict Set IfExp JoinedStr NamedExpr AugAssign Pass Assert Raise Starred SetComp ...`) or a named reason: `decorator`, `def_signature` (positional-only / keyword-only / `*args` / `**kwargs` parameters; defaults are allowed), `annotation`, `else_clause` (`if` / `for` with an `else` or an `elif`: an `elif` is an `else` holding an `if`, and its `else:` line starts no statement of its own), `expr_statement` (an expression statement that is not a call, e.g. a docstring), `star_import`, `star_args` (`f(**k)`), `call:eval` ... `call:setattr`, `AsyncComprehension`. The argv is built from the task's relative file names (`tests` is a list of relative `.py` paths validated by `normalize_task`; the bank carries no command line). ### LOOM-code open points

1. The ticket's own list of K1-K5 differs from design 10.2 (K2 an assignment using a constant, K3 a wrong-arity call that must be refused, K4 an undefined name, K5 a two-statement function with an import). 10.2 is not loose, so it was built as written; the ticket's K4 (undefined name -> definition-first refusal) is the careless K3 / K4 first try here, and the ticket's K3 (wrong arity -> refused) has NO static gate (design 5.2 has none): it is caught by the tests step only (exit 1), not refused at emit. A static arity gate (a call to a fixture def or to a def seated earlier in the thread, positional / keyword count against the signature; `arity_mismatch`) is about 60 lines and would make that K3 a typed refusal; owner's call.
2. The unsupported subset is much smaller than design L-LOOM-13's blocklist (it follows the ticket: def / return / assign / call / if / for / import, plus one list comprehension because 10.2 K5 needs it). No class, no `+=`, no `while`, no `else`, no dict / set literals, no `pass`. Too tight for real tasks beyond K1-K5? Widening is one line per node class in `code._ALLOWED_*`.
3. The shadow rule (L-LOOM-76) makes every token of the fixture a record, so `record_only` code tasks are possible only for tokens the fixture holds (e.g. `2` is NOT in this fixture and is constructed in K1). A weaver that does not look a token up before constructing it meets `constructed_shadows_record` for `x`, `(`, `:`. That is the intended "looked up" discipline but it is a cost in ops (K2: 62 rows).
4. The tests step needs a subprocess, so it is a harness step after emit with an `attest` row, not a gate at `emit` (the ticket's wording "a `tests` gate"). A run is complete (`status` / `emitted_output`) without it. The `attest` row shape is mine; LOOM-i should adopt or replace it. Network is not cut at the OS level.
5. Code tasks still name a prose `corpus` (`LoomServer` and `Run` require one; K runs build the fulllead Space, a few seconds per process). Not changed here; a code-only task would need `corpus` optional in mcp.py / ledger.py.
6. The emitted text is appended at the END of the target file; there is no insertion-position field (`context_names` = all top-level names of the target file). A position inside a file needs `target.after_line` and a context cut at that line.
7. Insertion into a class (a method) and nested defs inside a body are not supported: the thread is module-level statements, `def` bodies by depth. A `def` inside a `def` parses and passes (the walker handles the nested scope) but the context rules for it are untested.
8. `defined_in` is a hint for the model carried in the refusal; it names only non-import definitions, so a name defined in two modules lists both (≤ 3).
9. Files touched beyond the four named in the ticket: `verantyx/loom/mcp.py` (begin: build the index through the sandbox, `fixture` in meta.json) and `verantyx/loom/ledger.py` (replay: rebuild the index from meta.json's `fixture`); `verantyx/loom/state.py` is unchanged. New module `verantyx/loom/fixture.py` (the file-touching part; code.py must not open files) and `verantyx/loom/scripted_code.py`.
10. `PYTHONHASHSEED`, Python 3.11.14 of /Users/motonisihikoudai/vera-wiring/env. The header's `python_version` pins the full interpreter (L-LOOM-47); the builtins pin test is skipped on another minor version.

### LOOM-code review fixes: open points

1. The gates remain a blocklist and `typing.sys...` shows it: a stdlib module on the pinned list (`typing`, `operator`, `functools`, `re`, `json`, ...) hands out whatever it imported, and a string handed to `operator.attrgetter` / `methodcaller` reaches a dunder without a dunder `Attribute` node; `"{0.__class__}".format(x)` reads attributes through the format mini-language (reads, no call). The real answer is isolation (LOOM-d2: the Air or a container, no network, a throw-away user) and/or a per-module attribute allow-list instead of the stdlib list; narrowing `STDLIB_ALLOWED` is pinned by a test and was not done.
2. The tests step still runs on THIS machine, not the Air (design 9.4 and the compute-host rule), without `python -I` (the copy is on `PYTHONPATH`, which `-I` would ignore) and with the network open. `--isolation-confirmed` is only a recorded statement; `driver` is the caller's.
3. Two harness runs on one run folder give two attest rows (L-LOOM-84 iii): LOOM-i decides which one counts, or whether the second is refused.
4. Name rebinding passes (L-LOOM-84 ii); an arity gate (`arity_mismatch`) is a follow-up (L-LOOM-84 iv).
5. Non-`.py` files of the fixture (data files a test might read) are in neither `code_index_sha` nor `tests_sha`; `tests_sha` is over `.py` files only. The README is one such file.
6. The isolation token is stored verbatim in the attest row: the charset is limited, secrecy is not checked (the operator is told it is a label).
7. K1-K5 tests are placeholders (L-LOOM-84 i): no K result may be cited until codex's held-out tests replace them.

### LOOM-e results (2026-10-11)
Scripted baseline into `experiments/line3/loom/runs` and `results` (`harness.py run --driver scripted`, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, the 30 tasks of the bank): every ledger verifies (replay IDENTICAL); answerable I2-001, I2-041, I2-008, I2-034, I2-013, R2-I013, I2-025 = `hit` in `record_only`, `constructed_allowed` and `free_text` (21/21; constructed share 0 in every loom run); UF-001, UF-015, R2-U003 = `abstained_correct` in all three (9/9). The texts: ハッシュ表, キューバの太陽 (キューバ [record] の [foundation] 太陽 [record], c = {record 6, foundation 1}, stable at the first emit), カールマルクス, 1981年, 県社, ネパール, 青. Model rows per run (record_only): 12, 10, 12, 12, 7, 7, 7 for the seven answerable, 4 for each abstaining task; refusals 0; self-corrections 0. `hits_words` is true only for the single-unit answers (県社, ネパール, 青). These are the scripts' own words, a plumbing baseline, not the prediction test of design 10.1 (nothing was run on a model).
Tests: `tests/line3/test_loom_harness.py` = 34 tests; with the core's 197, `tests/line3/test_loom_*.py` = 231 passed under PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1 and 12345 (times: see the final report; the harness file alone is about 3 s). Covered: the task bank (30 rows, no gold, loads in the server); `.mcp.json` parsed and started as written (subprocess, sdk client: server name `vera-loom`, exactly the 18 tools in `MODEL_OPS` order); the agent files (tools = only loom tools, 18 / 18 / 3, `model: haiku`, no built-in tool name, no gold in any prompt); the T9 rule and its stricter views; every outcome class; a tampered byte -> `run_not_verified` (also through the CLI, exit 1); self-corrections on a crafted ledger; the demo tasks and I2-041 / UF-001 end to end through the harness (the worked example's output_sha values asserted); the whole scripted set; a control run; no overwrite; the subagent stub; a simulated subagent run scored from its folder alone (the free text with the gold of another task stores only its hash); determinism of the harness CLI under two other hash seeds (ledger bytes identical); the L2 driver with the fake client (tool calls only, text dropped with matching hashes, gold in free text scores nothing, `done`, 3 tool-less turns, tool_choice by model, run_id spoofing, a non-offered tool, API error, max_turns, the control, the SDK import confined to the factory).

### LOOM-e open points
1. `.mcp.json` names the owner's venv python by absolute path; it works only on a machine that has it (the harness test then skips with `ENV_MISSING[vera_wiring_python]`). A relative or `python3` command would find a different interpreter and, with it, `python_mismatch` on replay (L-LOOM-47).
2. The L1 path has never been run: the files load only after a session restart (docs/LOOM_SANDBOX.md section 2). Whether the subagent really cannot use any non-loom tool (T-LOOM-34) is checked by the operator against the recorder ledger, not by a test. `model: haiku` in the agent file and `model` in the Agent call are requests; the server only sees what the subagent declares in `begin` (testimony).
3. The L2 driver is untested against the real API: `strict: true` with the FastMCP schemas (`title`, defaults such as `tier: ""` on `add`, `depth: 0`, `pos: -1`) may be rejected by strict tool validation (all properties required, no defaults); a real call may need the schemas trimmed. Thinking blocks / `pause_turn` / `max_tokens` stop reasons are not specially handled (a truncated tool call is simply a tool-less turn). The choice of which models reject forced `tool_choice` is a list in driver.py (`FORCED_REJECTED`) taken from the API reference, not probed.
4. `hits_text` is a substring rule on the whole emitted text (design 10.1, the OP-F2-5 caveat): `excess_chars` and `hit_record_text` are reported so that a long or constructed text cannot pass unnoticed, but the result does not gate on them.
5. The first message of the API driver is the `begin` result as JSON, so the model never calls `begin` there; in L1 the model calls `begin` itself and declares its own model id. The two drivers therefore differ in who writes `begin.model` (the harness vs the model).
6. The control's server-side mode is `record_only` (L-LOOM-53); the control agent is told to ignore it. If the owner wants the server to know a mode `free_text`, `normalize_task` / `MODES` (core files) would change.
7. Scripted baseline results were written into the real `experiments/line3/loom/{runs,results}` (untracked); whether they are committed, moved, or removed is the auditor's call. Operator runs add random-id folders next to them. THE RUN FOLDERS ARE NOT PORTABLE: the server writes the absolute corpus path into the unhashed `meta.json`, so once the tree is moved or removed `verify` / `score` say `REPLAY_INPUTS_MISMATCH` (-> `run_not_verified`) until the path is given: `vera loom verify RUN_DIR --corpus FILE`, `harness.py score RUN_DIR --corpus FILE` (added; tested), or `meta.json` is corrected by hand. The test of `.mcp.json` starts the server, which creates its `--runs-dir` (an empty `experiments/line3/loom/runs/` in a clean checkout; no run folder, `begin` is never called).
8. Not built, as scoped: `tasks_code.jsonl`, the code fixture and `harness test RUN_DIR` (code tickets), the windows, the loops.

### LOOM-e review-fix open points
1. The transcript format is not documented by Claude Code; the parser is pinned to what 2.1.x writes and refuses anything else, so a new version may need the by-hand path or a parser update. Nothing was run against a real loom-weaver transcript (no restart yet, L1 never ran): the synthetic transcript has the shape of the real ones, not their loom content.
2. The T-LOOM-34 sidecar `transcript_check.json` and the `response_model` are testimony; the hash of the transcript file is in the sidecar, the file itself is not copied into the run folder (the operator may want to keep it next to the run).
3. The "surplus of model rows" test cannot see a parent call that replaces one the subagent also made, nor a call that leaves no row (`unknown_tool`, a refused `begin`; other refused calls DO leave a row and would show as a surplus); and the parent can call the loom at all while the server is allowed (L-LOOM-66).
4. `claude-mythos-5-1` is in `FORCED_REJECTED` beyond the reviewer's three ids (it is on the same API surface); drop it if the owner wants exactly three. An unlisted id that also rejects forced tool use ends in `api_error`, visibly.
5. The moved baseline results carry paths under `baseline_scripted/`; the pre-move results and runs are kept outside the repository (scratch) and can be discarded.
6. `hits_text` on the whole emitted text is still the rule (design 10.1); the answer-line rule applies to controls because their message is free text.

A gold entry carries `source_sids`, `from_evidence`, `pre_entry_hit` (a gold entry of an intra2 question before its article), `src_after_entry` (a cited sid beyond the evidence article), and per origin `(tier, seed, member, stability, unit, ratios, agreed, r2, r3, ratios_eval)`: `ratios` / `agreed` are `Candidate.end.status` / `.agreed`; `r2` / `r3` (the two ratio units of the I-11 agreement, a unit or None, never a float) come from the same reader the cycle used, `cy.Reader(facts, ctx.attached, ctx.energy_units).evaluate(ref.flat, ref.L)` of the ADOPTED state, one Reader per tier and question, and `ratios_eval` is that evaluation's status (a test checks `ratios == ratios_eval` on the toy); `arr` (stack: sha12 of `stack.arr_sha`; one-shot: sha12 of `Placement.to_bytes()`), `opened_at`, `closed_at`, `seated`, `read` (seed in `plan.read`), `seats_after_entry` (stack: seated units with a step > e(q)). Per tier: verdict, entries, `read` seeds, `unread` (the cap's `left_unread`), `would_read`, `tied_group_not_split` (`plan.boundary`), `rebuild_refused`, `rebuild_skipped`. `partial` is the cap's only (G4-c's L-G4-95); the stack's refusal is `rebuild_refused` / `partial_reasons`. | meter.py `measure`, `origin_rows` |
| L-G4-122 | 未着 (owner: excluded from the 現れる denominator and from the headline 2x2, counted apart). The scorer's own rule: an intra2 question is `unarrived` at a step iff NO unit of the arm's tiers in the prefix space holds a normalised gold alternative as a substring (`scorer.norm`, the rule of "gold in a candidate": a gold lies in one word of an entry, and the words are units). So a CHAR tier catches only a one-character gold, and a gold spelled by a PATH of several units is not counted (open point 1). Two flags per record: `unarrived` (the ARM's tiers) and `unarrived_3tier` (no RUN / WORD / CHAR unit holds it). For an arm that reads all three tiers they are one flag. For a CHAR-only arm (B, C_B) the 3-tier flag comes from the arrival step of every unit of a 3-tier stack (`Arrival`, the ledgers' `opened` lists; no tokeniser) and is NULL when that oracle did not load (it used to default to the arm's own flag, which silently calls almost every gold 未着 for B); the failure is printed, recorded in the meta (`arrival_oracle` {needed, loaded, source, error}) and shown in the markdown as a WARNING, and the tables then fall back to the arm's own flag, loudly. PRIMARY FLAG PER ARM (reviewer's recommendation; the owner will be told): `unarrived_3tier` for B and C_B (`events.PRIMARY_UNARRIVED`), `unarrived` for every other arm. The primary flag leaves a question out of the denominator in the step table, the events, the summary and the predictions; B's own CHAR-only count stands beside it ALWAYS (a second column in the step table, a row in the events table). A question whose primary flag is unknown is in neither the denominator nor 未着 and is counted as `unarrived_unknown`. Real data, 8 articles: I2-001 (gold ハッシュ表) is 未着 at every step for A (the tokeniser cuts ハッシュ | 表), I2-002 (連結成分) is not. | meter.py `measure`, `Arrival`; events.py `is_unarrived`, `flag_unknown`, `primary_key`, `events_of(key=)` |
| L-G4-123 | Events (7.4), `events.question_events`. Only the measured steps >= e(q) of an arm's records take part (L-G4-30). H_k = present-correct, G_k = gold in a candidate. appear = the first measured step with H; 直入 = appear == e(q) (delay 0); 後から = appear > e(q) while e(q) is on the arm's schedule, with the delay in articles and `late_input` (a gold entry that made H cites a sid after the evidence article, or its cross has a seat of a step > e(q)); a missing e(q) record of a scheduled step makes a later appearance a 後から, never a 直入 (the first version called the first measured step >= e(q) 直入, `i == 0`). When e(q) is NOT on the arm's schedule (arm C measures the Fibonacci steps only) the label is None, counted as `appeared_entry_unmeasured` and shown apart; `entry_measured` / `entry_on_schedule` stay in the events. The schedule is the set of steps that have a record of any question of the arm (or the planned steps, `events.scheduled_steps`). 残る = (n, m): the later measured steps that still have H, of the later measured steps (`stay`; the same for G, `stay_G`); `stay_all` counts the questions with H at every later step. A loss = H at one measured step and not at the next measured record. 戻る = H again after a loss. Never appeared, judged at the last record: 未着 (the primary flag), 非根拠 (gold in a candidate but none from the evidence), else the site tag, else 未特定. | events.py |
| L-G4-124 | Cause tags (7.4, OP-G4-3, owner: a recount 絞り is growth). The gold-holding crosses of the lost step j are the (tier, seed) origins of the gold entries that made H_j. At the loss step k each is R (its arrangement changed in (j, k]), else U (not in the tier's `read` at k), else A (read, no gold). 壊れる = the loss is a 単独誤答化 (verdict ANSWER, one entry, no gold, whatever the cause) OR has at least one U / A cross; 置き換え = not a 単独誤答化 and every cross is R; a mixed loss is 壊れる and keeps its tag multiset. A cross whose arrangement cannot be looked up is tagged `?`, counted as 壊れる, and reported apart (never silent). The arrangement oracle for a stack is the LEDGER (`LedgerArr`): a cross is rearranged in (j, k] iff a `grown` line of a step in (j, k] has `arr[0] != arr[1]` (充填 `filled`, 絞り `narrowed`, split into `narrow_new` = a unit left, and `narrow_recount` = left through the recount only), so the oracle needs no state load per step; a cross that only recorded units as left keeps its arr. For a one-shot arm it is the sha table of L-G4-119. The kinds are shown in the events table (the diagnostic column the owner asked for). A test checks the ledger oracle against `arr_sha` of the toy snapshots. | events.py `LedgerArr`, `cause_tags`, `question_events` |
| L-G4-125 | The site of a gold that never appeared (7.4: 未着席 / 未読 / 未採択), computed for every record that is present and not correct (`--site off` skips it; it costs one inverted index of the crosses' units per step, built in the parent). Question units = `ctx.energy_units` of the tier (the content units E_Q reads, stand-ins and function words excluded). Per tier: the crosses holding a question unit, the crosses holding a gold unit, `sited` = both, how many `sited` were read; tag 未着 (no gold unit in the tier), 未着席 (a gold unit exists, no sited cross; `closed_before` = a cross that holds a question unit closed at its budget while the gold unit co-occurs with its seed and is not seated in it), 未読 (sited, none read), 未採択 (a sited cross was read, no gold came out); the record's tag is the strongest over the tiers. It is a reading of the structure, not a cause, and it reads the ARM's tiers (for a CHAR-only arm its 未着 means "no CHAR unit holds the gold", not the 3-tier flag). | meter.py `site_analysis` |
| L-G4-126 | Resume, robustness and the config key. The result files are keyed by the run settings: `meter_<arm>.<key>.{jsonl,arr.jsonl,meta.json,md}` with key = sha12 of {grammar, effort, site, level} (NOT the code sha: with it in the name every edit of the code would start a new file and the refusal below could never fire); a run with other settings writes another file, and a directory with two keys for one arm is ambiguous to the renderer (`--key`). Every record carries `config` {grammar, effort, site, level, code_sha256}. A RESUME whose config differs from that of a record already in the file (in particular other CODE, or a record with no config at all) is REFUSED with `events.ConfigMismatch` (a typed RuntimeError naming the differing fields; the CLI prints it and exits 3; nothing is appended). A record already in the file for (arm, step, qid) is skipped; a worker error is a line `{"arm","step","qid","error"}` (qid null when a whole step could not be opened) and is retried on the next run; a line cut by a kill is skipped by every reader. FOUND BY A TEST: a cut last line has no newline, so the next append glued a new record onto it and lost it; `ensure_newline` terminates it before the first append (jsonl and, since the review, the arr table). A step with nothing to do is not even opened. A Pool is forked per step AFTER the index, the normalised unit lists, the inverted index and the grammar context exist, so the children share them. The file order of the records is the order of completion (not deterministic); every reader sorts by (step, qid), and the record bytes are (tested: 1 vs 2 workers, hash seed 0 vs 7, and an interrupted run equals an uninterrupted one). | meter.py `run`, `out_path`, `ensure_newline`; events.py `config_key`, `stem`, `check_resume`; tests |

A prediction is judged only for arms whose EVERY scheduled step is complete (69 intra2 + 25 unans at each of the arm's planned steps, `scheduled_steps` from steps.json; a hole at a middle step would change the 残る / 戻る series, not only the step-300 counts); P-4 only when BOTH A and C are there and complete; P-1 is "more than half of the appeared are 直入 AND 後から <= 5", judged on the worst and the best case when some entries are unmeasured (not judged if they differ); P-12 leaves out a question whose gold has a one-character normalised alternative (`one_char_qids` from the bank with the scorer's `golds`; not judged when the bank is not given). `meter_<arm>.<key>.md` shows the ones one arm can judge, `python events.py --summary` writes `summary.md` over all arms. P-7 is a structure fact (the closed share) and is not computed by the meter. | PREDICTIONS.md; events.py `judge`, `incomplete_steps`, `one_char_qids`, `summary_md` |

### G4-e/f cost of the full meter

THIN BASIS. The measured costs are 7 questions (I2-010, I2-025, I2-040, R2-I010, UF-005, UF-015, UF-020) at two prefixes of arm A (step 89 = 0.324 of the 592 sentences, step 300 = 1.0), one process each, `process_time` on the Pro at load 3-4, heavy-tailed (A at 300: 4.2, 181.7, 16.8, 3.1, 10.5, 113.8, 80.4 s = mean 58.6, median 16.8; A at 89: 3.5, 93.4, 1.3, 2.4, 6.5, 45.0, 92.0 = mean 34.9, median 6.5; the cost follows the LIST: the three expensive ones listed 121, 93 and 51 entries). B at 300: 1.3, 0.4, 0.4, 1.9, 0.03, 0.4, 0.02 = mean 0.64 s (one prefix only). C at 300 (grammar on): 219 s (I2-030) and 158 s (UF-010) = two questions. Opening a step: A at 300 32.3 s and about 5 GB resident in the parent (the stack state 6 s, the prefix space twice, the adhesion, the inverted index, the grammar context), at 89 14.3 s, B at 300 4.7 s, C at 300 1.3 s (the pickles).

THE COST IS SUB-LINEAR IN THE PREFIX. From 34.9 s at 0.324 of the corpus and 58.6 s at 1.0 the exponent is ln(58.6 / 34.9) / ln(1 / 0.324) = **0.46** (cost ~ c300 x f^0.46, f = the prefix's share of the 592 sentences). A linear-in-prefix extrapolation (exponent 1; the first version of this note, which called it an upper bound) therefore UNDER-estimates the small prefixes: it is a LOWER bound. The other bound is every step charged at the full step-300 cost (exponent 0). The sum of f^e over the 66 measured steps is 23.99 (e = 1), 37.56 (e = 0.46), 66 (e = 0); over the 13 Fibonacci steps 3.135 / 5.364 / 13. CPU hours = 94 questions x sum x c300 / 3600:

| item | linear (lower bound) | power 0.46 (the fit) | every step at the step-300 cost (upper bound) | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arm A, questions (66 steps, c300 = 58.6 s) | **36.7 h** | **57.5 h** | **101.0 h** | plan 8 estimated 75-207 h: only the every-step upper bound (101 h) lies inside that range, the fit (57.5 h) and the linear value (36.7 h) are BELOW it; wall at 2 workers about 29 h (18-50 h over the three), at 4 workers about 14 h (9-25 h); the tail is the 100-180 s lists |
| Arm A, opening 66 steps | - | about 0.3 h | 0.6 h | mean of 14.3 s (step 89) and 32.3 s (step 300) x 66; 66 x 32.3 s is the bound |
| Arm B, questions (c300 = 0.64 s) | 0.4 h | 0.6 h | 1.1 h | 7 questions, ONE prefix (the exponent is A's, assumed); against the plan's 45-124 h a 100x miss |
| Arm A0 (13 steps, c300 = 58.6 s) | 4.8 h | 8.2 h | 19.9 h | needs a foundation-off stack of 300 (not built; G4-d built A) |
| Arm C (13 steps, c300 = about 190 s) | 15.6 h | 26.6 h | 64.5 h | c300 from 2 questions (219 s, 158 s; the T10 flat/fast sweep layer0 over all 94: mean 186 s, median 167 s at load 5-70); C's own exponent is not measured (A's assumed); plus the 12 prefix caches (plan 8: 8.6 CPU h) that do not exist yet |
| **Arm C_B (13 steps)** | **7.0-8.2 h** | 12.0-14.0 h | **29.2-33.9 h** | reads the one-shot CHAR caches, i.e. the big one-shot crosses, NOT B's small closed stack crosses: the T10 CHAR tier at step 300 (94 questions) has median 86.4 s and mean 100.4 s per question (wall ms of a 10-worker sweep at load 5-70, so an overestimate of CPU); range 8-34 h, NOT the 0.3 h of the first version |
| Arm C_F at 300 | 5.0 h | 5.0 h | 5.0 h | 94 x about 190 s; f = 1, the three models agree; the g1_found caches exist |
| Arm A_rev at 300 | 1.5 h | 1.5 h | 1.5 h | 94 x 58.6 s; needs a reverse-order stack (not built) |

So: arm B (stack) is a run of minutes to an hour and a miss of about 100x against the plan, but ONLY on the stack, because its crosses are the small closed ones; the same CHAR-only read over one-shot caches (C_B) costs 8-34 h. Arm A is 57.5 h at the fit, i.e. below the plan's 75-207 h range (inside it only at the every-step bound, 101 h), not "2-5x cheaper"; arm C is as planned or above (26.6 h at the fit). All of these rest on 7 questions at two prefixes (A), one prefix (B), two questions (C): a basis that is thin and heavy-tailed, so the figures are orders of magnitude, not budgets. No per-question time limit exists.

Memory: A's parent holds about 5 GB at step 300 and the forked workers share it copy-on-write (a 16 GB runner holds A with 4 workers). The Pro's 4 workers of G-2 and this run must not overlap.

### G4-e/f open points (reviewer / owner)

1. 未着 is the scorer's rule on single units (a normalised gold alternative inside ONE unit of the arm's tiers). A gold spelled by a path of several units (the plan 7.4 says "and no path spells it") is not counted as 未着 here and not as gold in a candidate either (the scorer is per word), so it lands in 未着席 / 未読 / 未採択 / 未特定. Decide whether a path-spelling check is wanted. B's denominator now uses the 3-tier flag (the reviewer's recommendation; the owner will be told) and B's own CHAR-only count stands beside it; whether the owner wants the other choice is one `--key`-free change (`events.PRIMARY_UNARRIVED`).
2. Arm C needs a placement cache per Fibonacci step; only step 300 exists (f1b for the off arm, g1_found for C_F). `meter.py` writes an error record for a step without a cache (never builds). The 12 prefix caches, a foundation-off stack (A0) and a reverse-order stack (A_rev) are not built (G4-d built forward A only). For C the entry steps are mostly off the Fibonacci schedule: 直入 / 後から is then unknowable for C and shown as "entry unmeasured".
3. A's event `U` can dominate by construction: under the fast cap (4 crosses per tier) a gold cross leaves the read as soon as other crosses hold the question units (P-3 predicts that). The 置き換え / 壊れる boundary depends on `plan.read` being the cap's read; effort None would read all (the owner allowed it) but costs many times more.
4. The cost is heavy-tailed (lists of 90-120 entries cost 100-180 s, the median question 4-17 s). Nothing is cut: there is no per-question time limit; a GHA shard with a 6 h limit should split by (step range, question range) with `--steps` / `--questions` (both resume). The cost figures rest on a thin basis (see the cost section).
5. `events.stack_arr` reads the LAST snapshot's ledger; an arm built to step 300 serves any earlier record. A ledger of a shorter build (the 8-article smoke uses the 300 ledger) is fine: `changed()` returns None (a `?` tag) beyond its last step.
6. `meter_<arm>.<key>.md` embeds the arm's own predictions; the cross-arm ones (P-2, P-6, P-12) need `python events.py --summary` over a results directory that holds the other arms (and `--bank`, default the repository's bank). P-7 (closed share) is a structure fact from the G-2 ledgers, not in the meter.
7. NUMBERING: this block is L-G4-116..137. The tail of `line3` before it was G4-d2's L-G4-110..115 (G4-d: L-G4-87..95). `line3` still holds two L-G4-95 (G4-c's and G4-d's, see the note below); nothing was renumbered there.
8. The PREDICTIONS file was written before the first real-data run of the meter; the cost probes at steps 89 and 300 came after it. They happen to show present-correct records for A at step 89 (I2-010, R2-I010); they are not recorded as results and are not used for any judgement. The review changed what `judge` does with P-1, P-4 and P-12 (the rules above), not the registered texts.
9. When the primary 未着 flag of an arm is unknown (B or C_B without the arrival oracle), `render_md` falls back to the arm's own flag for its tables (with a WARNING), while `summary_md` keeps the primary flag, leaves those questions out of both the denominator and 未着 and shows `unknown N`; both show the failure, but they answer "what is B's denominator" differently in that case: read the WARNING, and re-run with the oracle. A results directory is keyed by the settings, not by the code: a full run that is stopped, has its code changed and is resumed is refused (`ConfigMismatch`); the choice is then to finish with the old code or to start a new `--out`. A CHAR-only arm in a checkout without the 3-tier stack (`--units-from`) gets a null 3-tier flag and a WARNING in its markdown; on a runner the stack cache must be present for B and C_B.
10. "One-character gold" for P-12 = a gold with some `|` alternative of length 1 after the scorer's normalisation (a CHAR unit can hold it); a gold of several characters is not excluded even though a CHAR path could spell it.

## LOOM-notes（型付き注記） (2026-10-11): the thread-wide consistency pass that points and lets pass — CONFLICT / UNANCHORED / NO_RECORD in the `read`/`emit` result and in a `loom_note` ledger row (renamed from `note`: 修正 L-LOOM-110), plus the self-correction metrics (ticket LOOM-notes of docs/LINE3_LOOM_DESIGN.md 12.2; owner 「気づきの置き方」 (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md), layers (2) and (3); verantyx/loom/notes.py [new]; verantyx/loom/{ops,mcp,ledger}.py [edited, small]; tests/line3/test_loom_notes.py [new, 52 tests; 72 after the review fixes, L-LOOM-113]; verantyx/line3/*.py, verantyx/loom/state.py and experiments/line3/loom/{harness,score}.py NOT touched; nothing committed; vera-impl/hidden never opened)

Built on branch `line3-loom-notes`, fast-forwarded from bf5261f6 to line3 738ed16c (LOOM-e merged), so the baseline is 409 loom tests (the review fixes below were made after merging line3 c93eb54d: G4-e/f and OP-LOOM-5) (364 + the 45 of test_loom_harness) and `experiments/line3/loom/score.py` (with L-LOOM-56 `self_corrections`) is in the tree. L-LOOM-85..94 are LOOM-d2's (another branch).

Three layers, never mixed: (1) prevention = the typed refusals of the core, unchanged; (2) notes = this section: structure points, the loom lets it pass; (3) noticing = `self_corrections` / `note_summary`, observation only. A note is never a refusal, never a score and never an input of the key.

The stored `read` / `emit` row is the result WITHOUT `notes`, byte for byte what it was; when the notes are non-empty the server appends a second row, op `loom_note` (修正 L-LOOM-110; first built as `note`), actor `loom`, right AFTER it (inside the same flock). A refused `emit` carries no notes (a refusal is not changed); a `read` is a dry run and shows them. Scope = the module or the body of one `def` / `class` (a nested `def` is its own scope; `if` / `for` bodies belong to the scope that holds them). Plain assignment against plain assignment is not a conflict (the K2 accumulator `out = 0 … out = add(out, x)` must stay silent); an identical definition or identical import repeated is a repeat, not a contradiction. The evidence unit `a` is the unit itself when it is a RECORD (`via:"self"`), and for a CONSTRUCTED unit the LONGEST PROPER SUFFIX of its surface that has arm evidence in the tier of its cross (`via:"suffix"`; a prefix is not an anchor because a particle follows the end of a phrase). Counts are the real `foundation.Adhesion.adj` of the corpus (distinct sids).
