## PUB-ACCEL (2026-10-16): the memory structure in C -- profile, incremental algorithms, C kernels, same bytes (verantyx/accel/, one dispatch hook in verantyx/loom/memory.py)

Owner decision (ops/decisions/2026-10-06_line3_faithful_build.md, last bullets): 「cで書いて高速化」, the C path must give the SAME BYTES as Python, the agreement of the two implementations is itself the correctness check.  Branch line3-cindex (from line3 a8296ae4); nothing in memcross / memdetect was edited (another agent works there): the change is NEW files plus one hook.

| id | decision |
|---|---|
| L-PUB-160 | THE PROFILE (this Mac, Apple silicon, Python 3.13, `nice -n 10`, the synthetic story of `m5m6/perf.py`, VERA_ACCEL=py).  Seconds per write (mean of the 100 writes up to the mark): 300 -> 0.064, 600 -> 0.161, 1000 -> 0.348 (the CI numbers of L-PUB-40 were 0.17 / 0.41 / 0.92 on a slower runner; the growth is the same, linear per write, quadratic per story).  cProfile of 10 writes at 1000 sentences (cumulative share of a write): `mem_state_sha` 35% (the loom state `to_obj` + canonical JSON, twice per write: the `prov.sids` snapshot of every unit makes the state 2 MB and O(n)), `build_corpus` 31% (adhesion records of ALL sentences 17%, `build_space` of all sentences and tiers 12%, then `Corpus.__init__`'s shas), `compute_write_notes` 25% (the gate hook `judge_memory` 19%: `judge_quote` x 3,400 per write; `conflict_notes` 5%), the weave 4%, the index fold (memcross, already incremental) 3%.  The same four items lead at 300 and 600.  Nothing in the hot list is arithmetic on Fractions: the (n, p, a) key computations (`seat_key`, `Weights`) are under 2% (their cache is per corpus, so it was rebuilt every write, but it is small); the sha of the 2 MB state is hashlib (C already), what costs is building the Python objects it hashes.  So the real win is ALGORITHMIC (do not rebuild what a write cannot change), and C is the second step on what is left. |
| L-PUB-161 | THE SWITCH AND THE HOOK.  `VERA_ACCEL=py` (default: the plain code, byte for byte the code of line3 a8296ae4) | `inc` (the incremental algorithms in pure Python, `verantyx/accel/inc.py`) | `c` (= `inc` + the C kernels, `vxcore.c` through ctypes; there is NO silent fallback: a missing library is `AccelUnavailable`).  The mode is read at every call (`accel.mode()`), an unknown value is a ValueError.  The hook is two lines at the end of `verantyx/loom/memory.py` (`from verantyx import accel as _accel; _accel.install(sys.modules[__name__])`): it rebinds `memory.build_corpus`, `memory.rows_bytes`, `MemRun.mem_state_sha` and, in memcross, `_rows_bytes` and `Corpus` (the per-prefix rebuild `build_index` runs at every commit and in every verify) to wrappers that call the plain function when the mode is `py`.  The wrappers re-implement three short functions; to stop a silent drift each plain function is PINNED (`accel.PINS`, sha256 of its source): on the first accelerated call a changed reference raises `AccelDrift` (read the wrapper against it, then re-pin; `memory._ACCEL_PINS()` prints the current values).  `VERA_ACCEL_CHECK=1` also runs the plain code inside every accelerated call (every corpus is compared object for object with `Corpus(bytes)`, every state sha and `rows_bytes` with the plain value) and raises at the first difference: the differential engine of the tests, as slow as `py`. |
| L-PUB-162 | THE INCREMENTAL CORPUS (`IncCorpus`).  The corpus of a write is the corpus of the rows before it plus ONE appended row.  Why that is exact: a sentence's units (three tiers, one splitter and one filter each) and its adhesion records (grammar `_build` / `char_records`) read that sentence alone, so `build_tier` over n sentences = the tier of n-1 with the n-th appended (postings tuples extended, dict iteration order kept: first occurrence order), and `Adhesion.from_records` over all records = the table of the first n-1 with the newest records appended (its sid is the largest, so its records are last in the sorted order `from_records` iterates; a count rises by one per key, the sorted counts dict is re-sorted only when a key is new, the evidence tuples and the weighted rows are extended / recomputed for the touched units).  Carried instead of rebuilt: the three tiers, the adhesion tables with their evidence, the placement `Weights` cache (minus every entry that names a unit of the new sentence, so a pair cached as weight 0 because a unit was outside the space is re-read, L-52), the `SpanIndex`, the particle-after index, and the gate's `evidence._VIEWS` entries (aliased from the parent's corpus sha to the child's, the grandparent's dropped: bounded memory).  `space_sha`, `adhesion_sha`, `seats_sha` are properties computed on first read (only a session's `begin` header reads them) and are the plain values.  The parent is found by what the SPACE reads (sentence, source, kind): `memory._write_v4` sets `clause_at` on the row it has just written and rebuilds, so the rows of the next write differ in bytes from the rows its parent was built from; only `corpus_sha` (the sha256 of the bytes, computed from the real lines) is new, the space is shared.  A tail of more than 8 rows, an unknown ancestor, a sibling (a refused write leaves another child of the same parent) go through the plain constructor or the append path and agree (tests). |
| L-PUB-163 | THE CANONICAL BYTES.  (1) `rows_bytes`: the canonical line of a row is memoised under every field `row_line` reads (kind, sent, source, topic_at, clause_at, turn, unshaped, weave_refused and whether each is present); a changed field is a changed key; a row the plain code refuses raises what the plain code raises (the plain `row_line` is the only writer of a line).
